articles.title: UCLA Replaces Athletic Director Martin Jarmond With Former Lakers Executive Tim Harris
articles.summary: UCLA has fired athletic director Martin Jarmond after six years and is replacing him with former Los Angeles Lakers executive Tim Harris.
articles.body: UCLA fired athletic director Martin Jarmond on Monday and replaced him with Tim Harris, the former longtime president of business operations for the Los Angeles Lakers. The shake-up was announced in a letter from Chancellor Julio Frenk to the university community. Frank described it as a "new path forward for UCLA Athletics." Jarmond, who had the job for six years, leaves immediately. The Bruins won three NCAA championships last season, including the first by the women's basketball team. Harris, 64, will have the title of CEO and athletic director and work on a pro bono basis, Frenk wrote. Harris graduated from UCLA in 1989 with a sociology degree and played goalkeeper for the men's soccer team while in Westwood. Harris spent over 35 years with the Lakers and left the NBA franchise in February, four months after the Buss family sold it to Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter. Harris was among Lakers governor Jeanie Buss' inner circle who received a major financial bonus after the sale. The team was recently sold again. Jarmond, 46, replaced Dan Guerrero as AD in 2020. He signed a five-year contract extension in May 2024. During his tenure, the athletic department has run yearly deficits for seven consecutive years, totaling $241 million in shortfalls. UCLA joined the Big Ten Conference two years ago, raking in millions of dollars in media rights fees while also facing increased travel expenses. Its deficit was reduced to $21.6 million for the 2025 fiscal year. The university has repeatedly bailed out the athletic department to keep it afloat. Frenk cited the financial situation as a reason for the change. "UCLA Athletics currently carries a significant financial debt, and its current path is not sustainable," Frenk wrote. "Now is the moment to build a model for Athletics that protects the breadth of our program, creates new opportunities for student-athletes and coaches, and supports itself through the revenue it generates." Frenk mentioned the rapid transformation of college sports in recent years, propelled by name, image and likeness deals that allow athletes to earn money. "UCLA must have an athletics model that leads — not just keeps pace," he wrote. Jarmond won't be around to see the debut of his last major coaching hire. Bob Chesney arrived in early December from James Madison to reinvigorate UCLA's moribund football program. The Bruins open the season at California on Saturday. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Hamilton hace realidad su sueño resucitando un Ferrari "cubierto de polvo y en un garaje desde hace más de 30 años"
articles.standfirst: El siete veces campeón del mundo de F1 ya tiene el coche de sus sueños: un Ferrari F40
articles.summary: El siete veces campeón del mundo de F1 ya tiene el coche de sus sueños: un Ferrari F40
articles.body: Era cuestión de tiempo que Lewis Hamilton acabara con un Ferrari F40 en su garaje. Ya quedó claro desde su mismísimo prmer día como piloto de Maranello (donde se fotografió con un uno), pero ahora parece ser que le ha surgido la oportunidad. Porque, por muy piloto de la Scuderia que seas, no es fácil conseguir una de las 1.311 unidades que se hicieron del modelo que celebraba el 40 aniversario de la fundación de la marca italiana que, además, se convirtió en el último gran Ferrari supervisado en vida por el commendatore. Sin embargo, parece que el heptacampeón británico ha tenido suerte y ha encontrado una pieza que, con la ayuda de los especialistas de Ferrari Classiche va a cumplir sus expectativas. Ahora, ha contado su historia en su Instagram. "Mi propio F40... es el coche de mis sueños, lo ha sido desde hace mucho tiempo, desde que tengo uso de razón. Desde niño sueño con tener uno. Y cuando me uní a Ferrari el año pasado quise poner uno junto a mí desde el primer día que pasé en Maranello. Eso demuestra lo que significa para mí". "Estos coches son obras de arte y muy raros, así que cuando encontré este, cubierto de polvo y en un garaje desde hace 30 años, supe que tenía que devolverlo a su casa. Primero, a Maranello, donde los ingenieros y mecánicos han trabajado durante semanas para devolverlo a la vida. Inmensas gracias a todos los que han echado una mano en este proyecto. Es un sueño hecho realidad... y no veo el momento de compartirlo con vosotros. Seguid atentos...", escribió. La histórica foto de Hamilton frente a la casa de Enzo Ferrari en la fábrica de Fiorano al lado de un F40 que marcó el inicio de su etapa de rojo no ha sido la única vez que le hemos visto junto al que es uno de los coches más admirados de toda la historia. Recientemente, aprovechando el Gran Premio de Japón de F1, el británico acudió a una reunión de aficionados a los coches deportivos en el mitico parking japonés de Daikoku. Nos brindó entonces unas instantáneas dignas de A Todo Gas, Tokyo Race, que luego tuvieron continuidad con otro post en el que le enseñaba a su pareja, Kim Kardashian, lo que el deportivo italiano era capaz de hacer guiado por manos expertas. Desde el momento en el que la restauarción/puesta a punto del F40 de Hamilton concluya, la estrella de Ferrari podrá disfrutar por fin de forma plena de los 478 caballos que entrega de V8 biturbo de 4,9 litros. Además, la cotización de ese Ferrari F40 en el futuro se disparará tras haber pasado por las manos de uno de los mejores pilotos de la historia del automovilismo mundial. Si el valor actual de ellos puede estar en torno a los 3 millones de euros... Muchos recordaréis que hace unos años Lewis Hamilton decidió deshacerse de su colección de coches en base a su conciencia medioambiental. Sin embargo, en algunas declaraciones posteriores abrió la puerta a romper esa norma con una excepción: precisamente el Ferrari F40. Ha llegado el momento y parece que va a dar para una amplia historia...

articles.title: Sandra Sánchez vuelve a competir
articles.standfirst: La mejor karateka de todos los tiempos anuncia que participará en la versión Master de los Juegos Mundiales en 2027
articles.summary: La mejor karateka de todos los tiempos anuncia que participará en la versión Master de los Juegos Mundiales en 2027
articles.body: Sandra Sánchez volverá a pisar un tatami de competición. La mejor karateka de todos los tiempos se retiró con un oro en los Juegos Mundiales de 2022. Cinco años más tarde se enfundará el karategui para disputar de nuevo este evento en su categoría Master. La campeona olímpica en Tokio anunció su regreso a través de sus redes sociales. "He recibido una invitación, he sido seleccionado y allí estaré. Nunca he dejado de entrenar y ahora lo haré también con ese objetivo", explicó la multimedallista de katas. Los Juegos Mundiales Master se disputarán del 14 al 30 de mayo de 2027 en Kansai (Japón). Están abiertos a deportistas de 30 años o más (sin límite superior). Reúnen 59 disciplinas de 35 deportes. Organizados cada cuatro años por World Masters Sport, la primera edición se celebró en Toronto en 1985, y la décima edición se celebró en Taipéi y Nueva Taipéi (Taiwán) en 2025. Esta próxima edición corresponde a la de 2022 que fue aplazada. Sandra Sánchez cerró su trayectoria deportiva con el oro en los Juegos Mundiales que era el único que le faltaba tras el logrado en los Juegos de Tokio, los dos mundiales (Madrid 2018 y Dubai 2021) y los siete europeos. Se retiró tras colgarse 60 medallas consecutivas y sin bajarse del podio desde 2015. Una trayectoria que ha llegado también a la gran pantalla. Este 21 de septiembre se estrenará 'Karateka' en el Festival Internacional de Cine de San Sebastián. La película, dirigida por Aritz Moreno y producida por Atresmedia Cine y Sr. y Sra, refleja con minuciosa fidelidad el camino recorrido por Sandra hasta convertirse en la la mejor karateka de katas de la historia. La historia, protagonizada por Andrea Ros y Patrick Criado, llegará el 30 de octubre a las salas de cine de la mano de Warner Bros.

articles.title: BBC's Ski Sunday to end after nearly 50 years
articles.summary: The BBC is to end its Ski Sunday programme after nearly 50 years.
articles.body:
Ski Sunday, the BBC's winter sports programme, is to end after nearly 50 years.

First broadcast in 1978, it featured the best of winter sports action, with Ed Leigh and Chemmy Alcott its most recent presenting team.

"Changing audience behaviours and the tough financial decisions needed to meet savings requirements mean BBC Sport must continually review how it delivers value for licence fee payers and serves audiences across all platforms. This decision forms part of that process," said a BBC Sport statement.

Philip Bernie, head of BBC Sport events, said Ski Sunday "has been a truly iconic programme".

He added: "Generations of viewers have enjoyed its coverage of the best in winter sports.

"We are enormously proud of the role it has played in bringing these moments to audiences across the UK, and extremely grateful to the brilliant people who have delivered them, not least the current outstanding team.

"These decisions are never easy, but as audience viewing habits evolve and we work to deliver value for licence fee payers, we have to make tough choices.

"We remain committed to bringing audiences the very best of winter sport, above all at the Winter Olympics, across BBC Sport's platforms."

articles.title: Fantasy Football Roundtable: 6 sleeper RBs our Yahoo analysts are prioritizing in 2026 drafts
articles.summary: Our analysts give you their favorite RB sleeper for the 2026 fantasy football season.
articles.body:
Running back is a position that can make or break your fantasy football team each season. Whether it's due to injuries, a decreased role or emerging players on the depth chart, RBs can rise and fall at any given moment. While it's important to prioritize the position early in your draft, it's also not one to ignore later on. Yahoo analysts Hayden Winks, Joel Smyth, Josh Norris, Justin Boone, Matt Harmon and Scott Pianowski give you their favorite RB sleeper for 2026.

Mike McDaniel curated the most explosive rushing offense of the decade with a bad OL and QB. We'll see what he can do with better OT and QB play this year, but there's a lot of reason to be excited about Mitchell fitting into the mix. McDaniel put Mitchell on a "WANTED" poster this free agency, as his pure speed is built for this perimeter and misdirection scheme. Mitchell is the RB1 in rush yards over expected (+47%), RB1 in EPA per carry (+0.12) and RB2 in YPC (6.3) among RBs with 100+ carries since 2023. Huge efficiency numbers are the expectation, not the ceiling. If he eats into Omarion Hampton's workload, Mitchell could sneak into the flex radar. If Hampton misses time, Mitchell would be very fun. I've enjoyed watching Mitchell be experimented with as a receiver, too. They've been sending him on wheel routes and swing passes throughout camp and the preseason. Let's just hope the injury he's currently dealing with isn't serious. — Hayden Winks

Going off the board around 78th pick, Rhamondre Stevenson may not be the typical sleeper of a young player about to rise on the scene, but he is an underdrafted player who can produce once again. Fantasy football ends in Week 17, but the most important football comes afterwards. From Week 18 to the end of the playoffs, Stevenson averaged 16.1 half-PPR PPG on a struggling offense. There hasn't been much TreVeyon Henderson has done better than Stevenson. Not only is Stevenson more efficient, but was one of the most efficient runners in the NFL, while being one of the best pass blockers at the position, reliable in the red zone and hasn't fumbled in 13 straight games. New England trusts him too much to take him off the field for the important plays, yet the threat of Henderson opens the door to drafting a team's RB1 on a top offense in Round 7. — Joel Smyth

Do I think it's probable that Mike Washington Jr. turns this backfield into a 50-50 split? No. Do I think it's possible? Yes, and no one else seems to be discussing this outcome. We still know very little about Ashton Jeanty's prayer circle-inducing ankle sprain. If it limits him in the opening few games of the season, Washington will have a larger role to showcase his immense talent. His explosiveness and underrated vision/footwork at the line of scrimmage has been on full display during the preseason. And if that continues to pop up against the Dolphins in Week 1, the Raiders' easiest opponent in the opening seven games, Jeanty's 84% market share of the team's backfield touches could be cut down to 65% — an outcome that would have seemed surprising a few weeks ago. In short, I believe Washington is too good to limit to five touches per game. And if Jeanty misses extended time at all this season, you are staring at a top-18 weekly running back in rankings. — Josh Norris

You rarely get an opportunity to select an NFL starting running back in the ninth round or later, but Croskey-Merritt is still going off the board in that range. While his ADP was suppressed earlier in the offseason by the uncertainty around Rachaad White's role in the Commanders' offense, several beat writers have made it clear that JCM answered the challenge from coaches to step up in the passing game and will get the first shot at leading this backfield. Fantasy managers will remember his contributions well, since he was the RB10 in fppg during the fantasy playoffs, topping 95 yards on two occasions and scoring four touchdowns over that stretch.

The 25-year-old is also a good fit in new offensive coordinator David Blough's scheme, which should feature more zone runs. Among 65 qualified backs last year, Croskey-Merritt finished eighth in zone yards per carry and 13th in success rate on zone runs, per Fantasy Points. Though the injury to star tackle Laremy Tunsil adds uncertainty to Washington's offensive outlook, the Commanders RBs will have the benefit of the sixth-easiest fantasy schedule . Even with White working in on passing downs, Croskey-Merritt is the type of explosive ball carrier who can deliver week-winning fantasy performances. — Justin Boone

The more I've looked at this Vikings offense, the more I buy the narrative that the team will really commit to the run game. They've given lip service to it before; this year it's for real. Minnesota hired Frank Smith to come over from the vaunted Dolphins run game to refurbish their own ground attack. It was sorely needed. The Vikings also added some heavy bodies to the mix this year, such as fullback Max Bredeson and power slot receiver Jauan Jennings. There are more "in the box" blockers than in the previous version of this offense.

Quarterback Kyler Murray is only with the team on a one-year deal, and there's been talk about him being heavily used as a designed runner. That can open up lanes for the backs. Jordan Mason is the best bet to severely outkick his ADP of the group, as the competition is an aging Aaron Jones Sr. and a sub-190-pound rookie in Demond Claiborne.

Last year, the Dolphins, where Smith came from as the offensive coordinator, ranked 12th in zone rushing rate but second in yards per carry on gap runs, as they integrated those in Mike McDaniel's usual bread and butter to hunt for explosive plays. In 2025, Mason ranked 19th in success rate on zone runs and second on gap runs (minimum 100 rush attempts), per Fantasy Points Data. There's some "fell for it again" risk with Mason but he's a sensible sleeper bet going outside the top-100 picks. — Matt Harmon

Kyren Williams remains the featured back in Los Angeles, no changes there. But make room for Corum in the Circle of Trust. Corum averaged double-digit carries for the final 11 games of 2025, producing at a pace that maps to 179-911-7.7 for a full season. The Rams could turn this backfield into a 60-40 split for the fresh season, which would give Corum standalone value from the jump. articles.title: Fantasy Football: The keys to starting the season strong — and boosting your playoff chances from the jump
articles.summary: Getting off to a hot start is one of Scott Pianowski's keys to succeeding in fantasy football.
articles.body:
You're an engaged fantasy football manager. You've been scouting all summer, thinking about skills and roles and strategies and the like. You've been dreaming of that championship at the end of the year, the glory and the parade.

Let me introduce another word for you: leverage.

Any large journey begins with small steps, and that's my goal for today — small steps. I prefer to attack fantasy football with a microscope, not a telescope. It's such a snow globe league, sure to look radically different in a few months. So my initial aim is to consider what I know right now and do my best in the short term.

I want you to dominate early in the fantasy football season. That's the cleanest way to prepare for glory later in the season.

A fast starter in fantasy football affords you that leverage, and with that comes wonderful things. Maybe you can shrug off a difficult bye week. Perhaps you can make some of those obvious 2-for-1 trades where you're sacrificing depth to a desperate opponent and poaching their star. In the middle of the year, we can start shaping a roster that's set up to dominate in the money weeks, armed with more reliable information on which defenses truly are horrible.

If you have leverage, you can let the game come to you. If you don't have leverage, you often find yourself forcing things, pressed into an activity you would prefer to avoid.

How do we play for today? How often do fast-starting or slow-starting teams make the playoffs? Here are some concepts to consider:

A fast start doesn't guarantee a playoff spot and a slow start doesn't doom you for the year. But let's see how the actual math shakes out:

Obviously you're more likely to have a strong team if you start fast, and your roster might have holes if you start slowly. But a quick start also brings that leverage we talk about; the freedom to be patient with a bench player or the luxury of mining the waiver wire without "must-win" challenges staring you in the face. Fantasy football leverage is like being on the button in every poker hand you play. It's a cheat code.

I'd prefer not to draft into injuries in August — I know injuries will find me soon enough early in the season. Jordyn Tyson should have a terrific pro career, but when his hamstring injury fell this summer, he essentially dropped off my draft board. I'm not waiting two months for a player with zero track record.

Injury optimism is rarely your friend in fantasy football. A hurt player might need a prove-it week or two before you feel confident starting him. Perhaps they'll be on a limited snap count when they return. The picture often takes too long to develop. Alec Pierce was dinged up all summer; I love the player, but I won't take him either. I don't want to be guessing in September.

Obviously your roster needs to be a collection of balance — your best players will help you all year, while the remainder of your roster could be a mix of help-now and help-later players. J.K. Dobbins should be the early backfield winner in Denver, holding off RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman. David Montgomery has a favorable rushing schedule for the opening weeks. Omarion Hampton should hit the ground running against a favorable opening slate.

This is more of that "microscope, not telescope" way of thinking. Again, you need a mix of cadence-specific players on your roster. It's fine to do some long-term planning, too. But sometimes it's important to realize value that's immediate.

Opponents don't come into play with your superstars, of course — if you're rostering Bijan Robinson or Puka Nacua or Trey McBride, you're rolling them out against all comers. But the matchups are critical at the lesser positions and the streamable spots. In most of my leagues, I'll have a short leash for my D/ST picks and often rent them out, a week at a time.

Week 1 already is giving us some signals. The Chargers are 10.5-point favorites over the Cardinals, the Lions are 7-point favorites over the Saints and the Jaguars are a 7.5-point choice over the Browns. I will aim to draft one of these three favorites for my Week 1 defense, and I don't suspect any of these D/ST targets will be that expensive.

One of the biggest mistakes fantasy managers make is to overly fall in love with their bench. Obviously, it's a season-to-taste thing; I'm not saying you have to recklessly cut players without a thoughtful moment or two first. But in-season information often means more to us than blind summer speculation.

Are you familiar with the Monty Hall Problem ? It's a counter-intuitive logic puzzle that shows us that when we have additional information, it's often in our best interest to change our mind.

We can take that concept and apply it to our fantasy world. Once the NFL starts playing real games, the Monty Hall Problem applies to fantasy football; with more information, changing is often the correct choice. (This is not to be confused with the 2014 Denver Broncos ; that was the Montee Ball Problem .)

articles.title: A big deal has been clinched as Manchester City give Enzo Maresca the midfielder he wants
articles.summary: Perhaps the most prolonged transfer of the summer was the potential move of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea to Manchester City. At one point, Chelsea imposed a d...
articles.body:
Perhaps the most prolonged transfer of the summer was the potential move of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea to Manchester City. At one point, Chelsea imposed a deadline on any club to move for the Argentinian international. That deadline passed without City, or any other club, moving for the Chelsea midfielder. Then, the move entered a holding pattern as it was expected that City would make their move to sign Enzo Fernandez. However, Manchester City's move never arrived until late last night . Now City have sealed the deal to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. In the process, they have given Enzo Maresca the midfielder he desperately wanted to bolster his squad.

Enzo Fernandez will join Manchester City after they have agreed a deal to sign him from Chelsea.

Manchester City have finally agreed to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. Fabrizio Romano reports that City will sign the Argentinian midfielder for over £125 million after lengthy negotiations between the two clubs. It is also reported that Enzo Fernandez only wanted a move to Manchester City and is now set to undergo his medical with City.

David Ornstein has reported for The Athletic that Manchester City have equalled the British transfer record to sign Enzo Fernandez. Ornstein reports that City will pay £125 million to sign the Chelsea midfielder. Lastly, Ornstein adds that the deal that will see Enzo Fernandez join Enzo Maresca's squad equals what Liverpool paid to sign Alexander Isak from Newcastle United last summer.

Despite the controversy surrounding Enzo Fernandez, he will add qualities that City need in midfield.

Manchester City have basically completed their midfield rebuild by signing Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. The Argentinian international is one of the elite midfielders in the Premier League and he will bring attributes that City need in midfield. Yes, Enzo Fernandez is a divisive character due to the past controversies he has been involved in. Focusing solely at what Enzo Fernandez does on the pitch he will add tremendous quality and a specific set of attributes to City's midfield.

Enzo Maresca primarily used Enzo Fernandez at Chelsea as an advanced number eight or as a number ten. The Argentinian midfielder became somewhat of a creative force playing under Maresca for Chelsea. His ability to score goals and create for others grew, which is an attribute that Maresca would like to tap into at City. All told, Enzo Fernandez scored 15 goals and added 19 assists in 79 matches playing under Maresca at Chelsea.

In possession, Enzo Fernandez is a quality midfielder. He links the ball exceptionally well and can be a line breaker with his passing. The Argentinian international typically operates best when utilised as a deep-lying playmaker. His passing range and ability to control the tempo of a match will mesh well with what Manchester City already have in midfield.

The biggest concern with Enzo Fernandez as a player is his work out of possession. He can caught out possession and his ability to win duels isn't considered elite. However, if Maresca were to pair Enzo Fernandez with Elliot Anderson or Ayyoub Bouaddi this would cover this deficiency in the game of the World Cup winning midfielder.

Also, Enzo Fernandez does have a nasty side to his game. He can turn to the 'dark arts' which can draw the ire of the referee and his opponents. However, playing on edge does bring out the best in Argentinian midfielder.

Manchester City have finally landed the midfielder that Enzo Maresca desperately wanted by agreeing a deal to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. Manchester City's signing of the controversial midfielder will divide opinion, but what isn't in doubt is the quality that Enzo Fernandez will add to Manchester City's midfield. Also, Fernandez will always give 110% commitment. While his signing is expensive, it could be looked back upon as a shrewd piece of business by Manchester City.

articles.title: Tony Romo breaks silence on CBS status for first time since OWI arrest
articles.summary: CBS broadcaster and former NFL QB Tony Romo is speaking out for the first time since his arrest in July.
articles.body:
Tony Romo remains on leave at CBS as the NFL regular season approaches, following a July arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, but he is speaking out for the first time since his status at the network came into question.

Romo released a lengthy statement on Tuesday, explaining his side of the story and the steps he has taken since his arrest.

Romo's comments also hint at his future alongside Jim Nantz at CBS, which has been up in the air since his placement on leave.

Romo said in a statement that he pleaded no contest to a civil offense for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

"Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain," Romo said. "That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol."

Romo called his arrest a "personal failure" and said he has spent the past month confronting his own mistakes.

"I am working closely with a team of doctors to address and make the necessary changes," Romo said.

The former quarterback thanked his family and friends, as well as the NFL community, for their support since his arrest in Wisconsin on the evening of July 23.

Here's what Romo had to say about his future at CBS.

Romo didn't make any definitive statements about his broadcasting job, but he strongly hinted that he plans to return to the booth.

"As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period," Romo said.

Romo appears to be expecting CBS to bring him back when he is ready, but his statement indicates he isn't planning an immediate return. With Week 1 less than two weeks away, that means J.J. Watt is in line to open the season as CBS' No. 1 color commentator next to Jim Nantz. Nantz's team is calling the NFC North matchup between the Packers and Vikings in Week 1.

articles.title: Jalen Duren Seeking Over $40 Million Annually As Pistons Offer $35 Million
articles.summary: Jalen Duren reportedly wants more than $40 million annually, but a rival executive believes his camp is being unrealistic.
articles.body:
Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are still in a contract standoff, with the All-Star center reportedly wanting more than $40 million per season, while the Pistons are ready to give him an offer in the $35 million per season range.

According to ESPN's Tim MacMahon , league sources say that the Pistons are ready to offer him a five-year contract in the range of $35 million annually, and that would put the contract at around $175 million. But Duren is looking for an average annual salary exceeding $40 million . That means he's seeking a contract exceeding $200 million.

But an executive from an Eastern Conference rival thinks that Duren's camp might just be asking for too much.

"Duren and his agent aren't being realistic. They're anchored to the max-type offer. But $35 million is not a discount. It's a lot of money."

Duren clearly has a good argument after having the best season of his career. The 22-year-old averaged 19.5 points and 8.5 rebounds last season, earning his first All-Star selection and making the All-NBA Third Team, while helping the Pistons finish with a 60-22 record and securing the number one seed in the Eastern Conference.

His postseason performance was less than spectacular. Duren averaged just 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds during the Pistons' playoff run, which is one of the main reasons the Pistons have yet to offer him the contract that he wants.

Duren is technically qualified for an even bigger payday by making the All-NBA team. The Rose Rule makes him eligible for a five-year, $287 million extension, but the Pistons have reportedly said that figure is a non-starter. The Pistons have made sure that they have kept every team away from any sign-and-trade scenarios , even though there are several teams that have been linked to him .

The comparison with other highly paid centers might also explain the Pistons' position. Only Nikola Jokic , Joel Embiid , Karl-Anthony Towns , Domantas Sabonis , Rudy Gobert , and Alperen Sengun are set to make more than $35 million next season among centers.

Meanwhile, only three players from Duren's 2022 All-Star class, Paolo Banchero , Chet Holmgren , and Jalen Williams , have received a 25% rookie max extension and will make $41.2 million next season.

From Duren's point of view, his All-NBA selection gives him a proper reason to be paid within that same range.

The Pistons' hesitation is about more than Duren. The president of basketball operations, Trajan Langdon, is also trying to keep enough flexibility to make sure that they can pay Ausar Thompson next season and maintain a championship-level supporting cast around Cade Cunningham .

The second apron rule makes overpaying even one member of that core very costly and could possibly force the Pistons to break up their team.

Duren does have a small piece of leverage. He can accept his $9.6 million qualifying offer, play out the season, and become an unrestricted free agent next summer.

But that would mean walking away from $170 million in guaranteed money and accepting a massive risk that he can perform at a high level without injury next season.

With Detroit around $35 million and Duren above $40 million, the middle ground increasingly looks like the most logical way to resolve one of the NBA offseason's biggest remaining contract disputes.

articles.title: ‘The Past Month Has Been Difficult’ — Tony Romo Provides Major Hint on Broadcasting Future While Addressing Arrest
articles.summary: Tony Romo’s first public statement since his July arrest carried an unmistakable message about his broadcasting future: he still expects that future to inclu...
articles.body:
Tony Romo's first public statement since his July arrest carried an unmistakable message about his broadcasting future: he still expects that future to include CBS.

The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback, currently on indefinite leave from the network, addressed his health, his legal situation, and his career Tuesday. While much of the statement focused on taking responsibility, one sentence stood out for anyone wondering whether Romo believes his CBS tenure is finished.

Romo Signals He Still Expects a CBS Return

"The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant," Romo wrote , adding that he has been working with doctors while confronting his mistakes.

"As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period," Romo wrote.

That wording does not guarantee CBS will bring him back. It does, however, make Romo's own position considerably clearer than it was when the network placed him on leave July 31.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

CBS Sports president David Berson said Aug. 11 that the network was still assessing the situation and had "no timetable" for a decision. J.J. Watt has since been elevated to the lead NFL booth alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson while Romo remains away.

The uncertainty has also created a potentially expensive contractual question. Romo reportedly has four years and roughly $72 million remaining on his CBS deal. Mike Florio previously argued that if CBS attempted to terminate the agreement for cause rather than pay the remaining money, Romo could challenge that decision and trigger what Florio called a "massive legal fight."

PFN detailed that possible legal fight in August as speculation grew about whether CBS might use Romo's arrest as an off-ramp from the remainder of his contract.

Romo's Statement Changes One Part of the Equation

The possibility of such a dispute remains speculative. CBS has not publicly announced plans to terminate Romo's contract, and Romo has not said he intends to sue the network.

His new statement nevertheless cuts against the idea that he is preparing to quietly walk away.

Romo also disclosed that multiple back surgeries left him with constant pain and, in his account, contributed to a "dependence on pain medication." He said his efforts to stop using those medications led to an "over-reliance on alcohol."

"None of this is an excuse," Romo wrote. "These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them."

Romo said Tuesday that he pleaded no contest to a civil OWI offense in Wisconsin stemming from his July 23 arrest. CBS had already placed him on leave eight days after the arrest, and its most recent public position offered no timetable for his return.

That leaves two separate tracks moving forward. Romo says he is focused on his health and believes a return to CBS is eventually part of that path. CBS still controls whether that return actually happens.

For the first time since the arrest, though, there is little ambiguity about what Romo wants. He is not talking like a broadcaster preparing for an exit. He is talking like one planning a comeback.

articles.title: Raygun, la breakdancer olímpica viral: "Me sentía como una impostora"
articles.standfirst: Netflix estrena un documental de Rachel Gunn, la deportista australiana que se convirtió en uno de los fenómenos de los Juegos de París 2024
articles.summary: Netflix estrena un documental de la breakdancer australiana que se convirtió en uno de los fenómenos de los Juegos de París 2024
articles.body: Rachael Gunn llegó a los Juegos de París 2024 para vivir un momento histórico y terminó convertida en una de las grandes protagonistas de la cita olímpica. Bajo el alias de 'Raygun', la australiana se estrenó en el debut olímpico del breaking con una actuación que dio la vuelta al mundo y desató una oleada de memes, críticas y comentarios que trascendieron el ámbito deportivo. Horas antes de representar a Australia en la ceremonia inaugural, Gunn sufrió un grave ataque de pánico en la Villa Olímpica. El salto desde su vida cotidiana como profesora universitaria hasta un escenario compartido con la élite mundial del deporte había despertado en ella un profundo síndrome del impostor, tal y como desvela en el documental que Netflix dedica a la australiana dentro de su serie Secretos del Deporte. "Me sentía como una impostora. No podía parar de llorar... '¿Qué estoy haciendo? ¿Qué he hecho? ¿Debería estar haciendo esto?", confiesa Gunn a cámara. Con 38 años, Gunn había conseguido su plaza tras proclamarse campeona de Oceanía en 2023, pero su confianza se desmoronó poco antes de que se encediera el pebetero olímpico. En el documental, recuerda cómo rompió a llorar después de encontrarse con una cara conocida de la delegación australiana antes de la ceremonia inaugural en el Sena. Las dudas aparecieron de golpe. Se preguntaba qué hacía allí y si había tomado las decisiones correctas. Aquel episodio fue solo el principio de una experiencia olímpica. Gunn compitió menos dos semanas después y perdió sus tres batallas de la fase de grupos. B-Girl Raygun no puntuó, pero sus movimientos dejaron huella. Su baile, que muchos calificaron como el del canguro, arrasó en redes sociales. Se convirtió en un fenómeno mundial. "Fue bastante sorprendente cómo me convertí en tema de conversación en lugares donde nunca pensé que estaría", comenta Gunn. Su particular coreografía provocó una explosión de memes. Fue imitada en la NFL. Llegó hasta The Tonight Show Starring de Jimmy Fallon, fue mencionada por Adele durante uno de sus conciertos y generó incluso la defensa pública del actor Chris Hemsworth en el programa de Jimmy Kimmel. El primer ministro australiano, Anthony Albanese, salió en su apoyo y destacó su valentía por haberse atrevido a intentarlo. Junto a los memes comenzaron a circular informaciones falsas como que su marido y entrenador, Samuel Free, había formado parte del comité que decidió su presencia olímpica. "Fue realmente duro cuando se cuestionaban mi credibilidad, mi ética y mis motivaciones, así como las de Sammy", afirma Gunn, que vio como su salud mental se resquebrajaba. "Sentía que toda mi vida se desmoronaba ante mis ojos, y yo solo intentaba sobrevivir al día", dice en el documental que repasa su trayectoria hasta los Juegos. También se desvela por primera vez que durante ese período de preparación su madre sufrió tres aneurismas cerebrales y como Gunn comenzó un tratamiento con antidepresivos para controlar la ansiedad.. Gunn apunta también que, a pesar de lo que se llegó a decir de que tras esta experiencia dejaría el breakdance, nunca se lo planteó: "No sé de dónde salió eso. No dejaré que lo que pasó me aleje del baile. Me encanta el breakdance, siempre bailaré breakdance, siempre seré parte de esta comunidad".

articles.body:
Tony Romo seemed to indicate that he will eventually return to broadcasting at CBS in a statement Tuesday about his recent OWI arrest in Wisconsin.

Romo was pulled over on a Milwaukee highway in late July after participating in a nearby golf tournament and charged with OWI. In a statement published Tuesday on Instagram, Romo said he has pleaded no contest to the charge and that he had developed an "over-reliance on alcohol."

"Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain," Romo wrote, in part. "That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol."

Nevertheless, he said that this was not an "excuse" and that he takes "responsibility" for the incident.

Romo was placed on indefinite leave by CBS after the incident. JJ Watt has been elevated to the network's top NFL team with Jim Nantz, and Ross Tucker is working with Ian Eagle on the second team, where Watt called games last year.

It has been an open question as to if or when Romo will return to CBS at all. CBS Sports president David Berson told reporters in August that he was still "assessing" the situation and that there was no timetable or "final decision" as to whether Romo will come back.

In his statement on social media, Romo seemingly indicated he will be back with CBS one day.

"I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes," he wrote. "I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know. As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period."

Many former athletes have described a painful cycle of surgeries and prescription medications in their retirement years. Romo's account resembled the later years of Tiger Woods's career; Woods sought treatment after a recent DUI after years of prescription drug use to deal with pain from back surgeries.

Plenty of questions remain for Romo. When will he be back on the air for CBS? We don't know. Will CBS bump him to a No. 2 analyst job and keep Watt No. 1? That's to be determined. More importantly, will CBS keep Romo at all? Or use his arrest, and embarrassing police-cam video, as an excuse to exercise a morals clause in his contract and wriggle out of the four years and $72 million remaining on his contract?

CBS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: Fans Slam ESPN After Trinity Rodman Is Introduced as Ben Shelton’s ‘Girlfriend’ at US Open Match
articles.summary: Rodman and Shelton confirmed their relationship in March 2025
articles.body:
Fans called out ESPN for introducing Trinity Rodman as "Ben Shelton's girlfriend" as she was shown at his US Open match on Monday

"There's Trinity Rodman, also known as Ben Shelton's girlfriend, and also known as a member of the US Women's National Team," the broadcast said

Rodman made her USWNT debut in 2022 and has since won Olympic gold

Fans were not happy with the way Trinity Rodman was introduced at the US Open.

Rodman, 24, was in the stands at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Monday, Aug. 31 as her boyfriend Ben Shelton faced Tallon Griekspoor of the Netherlands in the first round.

"There's Trinity Rodman," ESPN broadcasters said, "also known as Ben Shelton's girlfriend, and also known as a member of the US women's national team."

The chyron on the screen read, "Ben's girlfriend & USWNT player" as Rodman was shown in the stands.

As ESPN's cameras pointed to her, the Washington Spirit star was all smiles and appeared to be joking with her seatmate.

Fans called out the introduction in the comments of ESPN's Instagram post of the moment. "You forgot Olympic gold medalist," said one commenter. "Trin is an Olympic gold medalist, NWSL player and then Ben's girlfriend. In that order," said another with more than 3,000 likes.

Another user responded to that comment, writing, "thisssss come on @espn @espnw do better!!!!"

An additional comment read, "How about just say her credentials and then let the commentators mention she just happens to also be Ben's girlfriend. 🙄"

Rodman, who has been on the USWNT since 2022, won an Olympic gold medal with the squad at the 2024 Paris Games, scoring three goals and one assist during Team USA's gold medal run. She currently plays for the Washington Spirit in the NWSL, after fighting to increase salaries for the league, and was named rookie of the year in 2021.

Rodman hasn't commented on the fan outrage this year, but during the 2025 Wimbledon Championships, the soccer star called out broadcasters for mixing up her name and focusing on her estranged father, former NBA star Dennis Rodman .

"For those who don't know, my name is TRINITY not Tiffany," the Washington Spirit forward wrote on her Instagram Stories. "Also, for Ben's matches, he has his family there as his support system, which includes his dad… my dads not even in MY life no need to bring him up during HIS matches when I don't even want him talked about during mine. It's his and his loved ones' moment. Thank you."

Shelton won his match on Monday and will next play Hubert Hurkacz on Wednesday, Sept. 2.

articles.title: Lakers predicted to sign $15M extremely athletic former first-rounder to pair with Luka Doncic
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are still looking to add to the roster. They could give this former first-rounder a real chance to revitalize his NBA career if they s...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers felt like they were very close to completing their offseason just last week after what has been an extremely interesting summer. The Lakers not only experienced significant roster turnover, but they also went through major organizational changes.

LA felt like it was going to land 23-year-old Jonathan Kuminga, and the move seemed inevitable.

"Jonathan Kuminga landing with the Los Angeles Lakers seems inevitable at this point. On Tuesday, it appeared Kuminga had three suitors remaining in his free-agent sweepstakes: the Minnesota Timberwolves , Cleveland Cavaliers and the Lakers," New York Post's Valentina Martinez wrote.

With the Lakers failing to sign Kuminga, they still have some major needs to address. Lake Show Life's Maxwell Ogden believes recently released Cam Whitmore would be a great addition to pair with Luka Doncic.

"As it stands, Whitmore has the catch-and-shoot proficiency to work off of Doncic and help the Lakers space the floor. He's also a bowling ball of a slasher whom defenders bounce off of as he makes his way to the rim and skies for highlight-reel finishes. If Redick can get Whitmore to buy in on defense, then Doncic's history of elevating his teammates' quality of play could be the up-and-comer's ticket to redemption," Ogden wrote.

Whitmore is a former first-round pick who simply has not panned out yet. However, he could be a strong fit with the Lakers. He was included in the Peyton Watson trade that sent him to Cleveland, but the Cavaliers ultimately waived him.

"The Cleveland Cavaliers have waived Cam Whitmore, league sources told hoopshype. Whitmore, the 20th pick of the 2023 NBA Draft, has averaged 10.5 points on 45% from the field and 35% from 3-point range in 17.3 minutes during three NBA seasons with the Rockets and Wizards ," HoopsHype's Michael Scotto wrote.

It would be a fresh start for Whitmore, and at this point, he knows he is beginning to run out of opportunities. Playing in an offensive system alongside Austin Reaves and Doncic could allow him to expand his game and maximize his scoring ability.

Whitmore was on his $15 million rookie contract before being released. The Lakers adding Whitmore would be an interesting move, to say the least. The team already has plenty of shooting, but adding a young, athletic scorer with something to prove would not be a bad idea.

articles.title: What Gary Player believes Scottie Scheffler needs to do more if he’s to be considered an all-time great
articles.summary: Gary Player is a huge admirer of Scottie Scheffler, both on and off the golf course. Player is one of the most successful golfers ever to have played the gam...
articles.body:
Gary Player is a huge admirer of Scottie Scheffler, both on and off the golf course.

Player is one of the most successful golfers ever to have played the game, with nine major championships to his name.

Amazingly, though, Scheffler is currently just two victories short of the South African's career PGA Tour win tally.

Scottie Scheffler has been the dominant player in the professional game for the past four years now.

And Gary Player is seriously appreciative of the Texan's accomplishments.

However, the 90-year-old wants to see more of Scheffler playing globally in the future.

What Gary Player believes Scottie Scheffler needs to do more

While speaking to Golf Monthly recently, Player suggested that he'd love to see Scheffler play more internationally.

" Scottie Scheffler is without a doubt the best player in the world today, and what I admire about Scottie Scheffler is that he's very much a family man. And your family is so vitally important, " Player said.

" I was deprived of that because I had to travel away from my family from South Africa. At least he's lucky he lives in America, he finishes a tournament, most of these guys have their own jets, they're back home on Sunday night and they can see them.

" But I would like to see Scottie Scheffler, who's such a wonderful golfer and such a nice man, to travel and promote golf internationally more than he does because we have a debt incurred.

" Golf has done so much for us and if Scottie would travel and play just a little more, I would say five tournaments a year like Nicklaus did, like Palmer did, like Sam Snead did, like Trevino did, like Tom Watson.

" I think he eventually will. I think at the moment he's so intent on setting as many records in America and I'll follow him with great interest. "

It is obviously Scheffler's prerogative to play more in America than he does internationally.

However, it would undoubtedly be great for the game of golf if he decided to play more international tournaments in the future.

What Scottie Scheffler said about playing more internationally

Back in July, Scheffler was asked whether playing more tournaments outside of the United States interests him.

" It definitely interests me, " the world number one replied.

" I'd like to see how it shapes out the next couple of years. There's a lot of places I think I'd like to play.

" There's always just, you know, the time and the place for me. I'm at a time in my life where I have a young family at home and young kids. The fall is a special time for our family. It's where we can really check out and be together, and I get to spend a lot of time with my kids. So I hold those moments pretty sacred.

" But at the same time I love golf and I would love to be able to play more internationally. Like Australia, New Zealand is a place we would love to be able to go to. My wife has always wanted to go to New Zealand.

" But like I said, I love this style of golf [links], and I feel like it's pretty unique to here. But going to play the Sandbelt in Australia would be pretty special as well.

" Hopefully I can find the time. It's definitely an intriguing part of the schedule and yeah, it definitely interests me, as well. "

articles.title: 31 Straight Wins: Has Ferris State Outgrown Division II?
articles.summary: Fresh off a 42-14 rout of No. 4 Pittsburg State and a 31-game winning streak, Ferris State is running out of things to prove in Division II.
articles.body:
At some point, dominance stops being impressive and starts raising a different question: What is left to prove?

Ferris State football may have reached that point.

The Bulldogs opened the 2026 season Thursday night by doing something that would have been difficult to imagine two years ago: they walked into Pittsburg State, the site of their most recent loss, and dismantled the No. 4 Gorillas, 42-14. The victory extended Ferris State's winning streak to 31 games and immediately reminded the rest of the country why the Bulldogs entered the season ranked No. 1 in Division II .

Pittsburg State handed Ferris its last loss, a 19-3 defeat on Aug. 31, 2024. Since then, Ferris has not simply won; it has crushed opponents on its way to consecutive national championships . Thursday's victory was particularly emphatic, as the Bulldogs ran for 385 yards while holding Pittsburg State to just 44 rushing yards .

Ferris State's résumé is becoming difficult for Division II to contain.

The Bulldogs finished 16-0 in 2025, defeating Harding 42-21 for their fourth national championship in five seasons. That made Ferris the first team in the modern era of Division I or Division II football to finish a season 16-0. The Bulldogs also scored 844 points, setting an NCAA Division I and II modern-era scoring record.

Four championships in five years is not a fluke. A 31-game winning streak is not a hot streak.

It is a program operating at an entirely different level.

That does not mean moving to Division I would be easy. Ferris would face larger budgets, deeper scholarship commitments, greater travel demands, and tougher recruiting competition. The university would also need to determine whether the financial and institutional investment makes sense.

But competitively, the argument is becoming harder to dismiss.

Ferris State has dominated Division II long enough that the next challenge may not be another Division II opponent. The next challenge may be Division I itself.

The Bulldogs do not necessarily need to move up tomorrow.

But after four championships in five years, a perfect 16-0 season and now 31 consecutive victories, the question is no longer whether Ferris State belongs among the nation's elite.

The question is whether Division II is still big enough for Ferris State.

articles.title: Manning, Bishop Jr. top Texas Longhorns to watch against Texas State
articles.summary: We are just four days from Texas football, and it's a big game for a few select Longhorns. Manning tops that list, looking for a clean performance.
articles.body:
As Week 1 game day approaches , the anticipation around the Longhorns "All-In" season continues to grow. Texas fully expects to get a rather comfortable win against the Bobcats this weekend, there are a few Longhorns that could use big weekends. Whether it's about confidence building or getting their first real-time snaps, there are five players I'm watching closely this weekend.

This is the obvious one. Fall camp reports haven't been as glowing as many expected around Manning. Well, Saturday is a chance to start to silence that noise. I'm less concerned with what the overall number look like to finish the day, with one exception: completion percentage. Texas should be able to run the ball, limiting Manning's ability to put up gaudy numbers on Saturday. However, an efficient, accurate performance is a must heading into a game against Matt Patricia and that Ohio State defense.

This has been the name of fall camp. The freshman WR has carved out a role in this offense and will see the field consistently on Saturday. A quiet performance would not set off alarms for me, but I'm fully expecting the freshman to shine this weekend. On top of that, WR depth can be an important piece for this offense playing at a high level throughout the season. Bishop doesn't need a great performance like Manning does, but I'm willing to bet he'll be well worth watching.

I believe this offense is going to be great this season. Nick Townsend could make it downright special. The best Sarkisian offenses at Texas have had a true receiving threat at TE(Helm, Sanders). Townsend seems to be the only TE with that receiving upside and it could shine on Saturday. Texas State is going to put so much emphasis on slowing down Cam Coleman, Ryan Wingo and Emmett Mosley V. That should allow these TEs, especially Townsend, to get loose for a couple of big receptions.

This is the most important piece to this weekend for me. I feel very confident in the veteran trio of Rasheem Biles, Justin Cryer and Brad Spence, but depth will be needed as soon as possible. This is the game where you can get Tyler Atkinson, Rocky Cummings and Kosi Okpala on the field consistently, letting them get their feet wet. At least one of those players will need to give the Texas defense snaps against Ohio State. I'll be watching closely to see who among the freshman trio can make a statement this weekend.

This is the position Texas fans will be biting their nails over. It seems Trevor Goosby isn't likely to play this weekend, so it will be Andre Cojoe in his spot. Obviously, this performance will be the baseline for this group but they should be dominant. Seeing confidence in both run and pass blocking, few missed assignments and some short-yardage success is a must for this game. Finally, and maybe most importantly, a game without pre-snap penalties would be very encouraging moving forward.

articles.title: ‘Last Chance U’ coach Buddy Stephens fired from East Mississippi Community College
articles.summary: East Mississippi Community College head football coach Buddy Stephens became a household name in the sports world and beyond as the centerpiece of the Netfli...
articles.body:
East Mississippi Community College head football coach Buddy Stephens became a household name in the sports world and beyond as the centerpiece of the Netflix documentary series Last Chance U . But his own last chance has come and gone as the school has decided to part ways with their longtime coach after publicly criticizing his own administration.

Last week, Stephens shared vocal criticism of his conference's new ten-game schedule that would complicate matters for teams that were hoping to play in the National Junior College Athletic Association playoffs. East Mississippi Community College has won five national championships during Stephens' 18-year tenure.

Stephens called administrators who made the change "idiots" and said that the reasoning was because the school presidents did not want to pay for travel expenses for the national playoffs via The Commercial Dispatch of Columbus, Mississippi. He also called the thought process behind the switch "junkified."

"Some of the presidents in the state didn't want to have to go to the national playoffs because they didn't want to travel the first week," Stephens said. "This is what really happened. If you really want to write something, write the truth – and this is what happened. The presidents decided they didn't want to have to spend a lot of money to travel, so they did our system, our playoffs and our yearly schedule in order for them to be able to back out of the (NJCAA) playoffs if they wanted to and stay in our playoffs. But if they were going to be a No. 1 or No. 2 seed and they were going to get to host and they didn't have to travel, then they'd get out of our playoffs and opt into the national playoffs so they can host."

Apparently, that quote was enough for EMCC to take drastic action. The school announced on Monday that Stephens would be removed from his position and replaced by offensive coordinator Preston Rice immediately. According to Football Scoop , Stephens did not coach EMCC's season-opening victory over Southwest Mississippi on Thursday.

Last Chance U. featured Eastern Mississippi Community College for its first two seasons in 2015 and 2016. Stephens' program and the documentary itself provided an incredible window into a world where the school wasn't just competing for a national championship, but where players were trying to prove they could do what it takes on and off the field to get a chance at the D-I level. It was raw, captivating, and unfiltered in a way that sports documentaries today just aren't.

While the series moved on to other schools for its final seasons, the story of Buddy Stephens and EMCC set the tone for the foundation of Last Chance U . And it will be fascinating to see where he goes next and what stories may come if he gets another chance to build a new program.

articles.title: Tony Romo breaks silence on OWI in lengthy statement: 'None of this is an excuse'
articles.summary: Tony Romo has finally spoken on his viral OWI arrest, as the CBS broadcaster released a statement on the matter on Tuesday.
articles.body:
It's been over a month since Tony Romo was arrested for Operating While Intoxicated (drunk driving) and on Tuesday, the CBS color commentator finally broke his silence on the viral incident.

In late July, Romo was pulled over in Wisconsin while attending a golf tournament and failed a sobriety test before being taken in for booking. CBS announced a few weeks later that Romo was being placed on leave for the incident but the broadcaster was not in any danger of being fired for the OWI. Former Houston Texan and CBS colleague J.J. Watt is set to step in for Romo in the booth alongside Jim Nantz while he is on leave.

While things have been quiet in the weeks since the news broke, a spokesperson for Romo did release a statement to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel after three new citations were filed in late August. The statement read : "Tony accepts full responsibility for his actions and has taken proactive steps to ensure that this isolated civil matter is properly resolved. We are working with local authorities to bring this matter to a close and we are communicating with CBS about next steps."

But on Tuesday, Romo himself finally issued a statement on the incident on his Instagram, breaking his month-plus long silence on the matter. In the statement, Romo explained that he has plead no contest to a civil offense and that he "own[s] this completely". Romo also elaborated on his personal health struggles after dealing with debilitating back pain that caused him to over-rely on alcohol to get by.

articles.title: What are big questions in final two days of Scottish transfer window?
articles.summary: How has your Scottish Premiership club fared in the latest transfer window?  After manager Martin O'Neill said he was content with his existing central defen...
articles.body:
How has your Scottish Premiership club fared in the latest transfer window?

Every side in the country has been able to strengthen the squad since 15 June. Some have been extremely busy, others not so much.

We are, however, expecting a late flurry of activity given clubs in Scotland can still do business until 17:00 BST on Thursday - a couple of days after England, and other leagues, have decided to wrap things up.

So where might we see some movement and which chairmen, chief executives and agents might be checking their phones nervously?

After manager Martin O'Neill said he was content with his existing central defensive options - Cameron Carter-Vickers, Auston Trusty, Liam Scales and Dane Murray - it was widely assumed Celtic would strengthen in the full-back position.

Especially with Canadian international Alastair Johnston ruled out until October at the earliest with injury.

There's also believed to be a strong desire to bring in a back-up to Kieran Tierney on the other flank, with Chelsea's 18-year-old Landon Emenalo a contender after his apparent tour of the champions' training ground at Lennoxtown the other week.

The mood music was that the player was nursing a knock and that the move would go through once he'd had further treatment. One to watch then, possibly.

Other names have been linked with the position, too, most notably Dundee United's Will Ferry and Motherwell's Emmanuel Longelo.

Cover for Johnston is currently being provided by Colby Donovan, with Tony Ralston also on the books. The extent of the Canadian's injury may determine how big a priority the club feels it is to bring in another right-back.

Further up the pitch, Celtic look fairly well off, given the arrival of midfielder Oliver Sorensen and with Joel van den Berg also seeming to be on his way.

But it will come as a major surprise if defensive reinforcements don't arrive in the window's final 48 hours.

The one thing that can't be faulted at Ibrox is the breadth of Rangers' transfer activity.

Since the window opened, 12 new players have arrived. Such is the volume, even die-hard supporters might struggle to name them all.

Without cheating, see if you can roll off the names... Godfrey, Nedeljkovic, Devlin, Shankland, Neil, Penrice, McCrorie, Yokota, Makhanya, Dragojevic, Pandur, Kim.

Quite the list, isn't it? And while some fans are already grumbling about the quality, the quantity represents pretty solid backing for new manager Derek McInnes.

Transfer number 13 needs to hit the ground running. Kevin Kelsy seems set to be that man and he has some pretty expensive boots to fill.

Rangers reportedly knocked back a bid well in excess of £20m from Turkey for Youssef Chermiti. The Portuguese striker then promptly got injured the same day and may be out for the season.

His replacement looks like being a 22-year-old 6ft 4in Venezuelan international who, after a couple of title-winning seasons with Shakhtar Donetsk in Ukraine, has been playing in Major League Soccer for the past two years.

While Rangers hit St Mirren for five in the League Cup, they've only scored six goals in their other seven matches. But with new wingers in the building, too, Kelsy should have plenty of service as the Ibrox club aim to be a lot more lethal in attack.

Hearts' captain left for Rangers. Their manager soon followed. As did stand-out midfielder Cammy Devlin. Another of last season's top performers, Alexandros Kyziridis, also departed for pastures new.

That left many a Hearts fan wondering whether last term's player of the year in Scotland would inevitably be the next to go. But at the time of writing, Claudio Braga is still wears maroon and continues to be a key cog in Vouter Wrancken's new-look wheel.

Can the club hang on to him for a further 48 hours?

The manager said he's spoken with his Portuguese talisman and that the pair are on the same page. He's keen to keep him but knows there are certain offers the club can't turn down - and certain teams or leagues the player wouldn't reject either.

The Tynecastle side have brought in Sabri Guendouz, Amadou Ba-Sy and JJ Williams to help strengthen a forward line that now also includes Calvin Miller and Josh McPake. James Wilson, too, seems to have returned a better player than when he left for his short stint with Spurs.

The retention of Braga, therefore, would be a real sign of Hearts' continued ambition to challenge the big Glasgow two.

Were he to leave, in addition to the big personalities from last season, the new manager's attempts to keep the club in contention at the top of the table is likely to get a whole lot harder.

So which clubs - and players - will be crossing their fingers that bids don't - or do – come in?

Dundee United may be caught between a rock and hard place over left-back Will Ferry. Keep an outstanding player in both boxes or cash in to the tune of around £2m for a player who arrived for nothing from Cheltenham Town two years ago? Anderlecht, Celtic and clubs in England have all been mentioned.

Hibernian could also be vulnerable to bids for two of their stand-out midfielders. Miguel Chaiwa and Josh Mulligan have both been the subject of significant interest this calendar year but both remain in green and white.

While Celtic have reportedly been keeping tabs on both, the Parkhead midfielder looks pretty full now if the imminent arrivals are confirmed.

Hibs are adamant no player is leaving until their valuation is met and are likely to be mightily relieved if both players are still in Leith come the end of the week.

Motherwell have already lost a good portion of the side that sparkled last season under Jens Berthel Askou.

Calum Ward, Elijah Just, Callum Slattery and Elliot Watt have all headed for pastures new. That leaves the vultures circling around last season's Premiership top scorer Tawanda Maswanhise, dynamic full-back Emmanuel Longelo, and tricky forward Ibrahim Said.

The Fir Park side have continued with the same attack-minded, fast-flowing football under new Swedish coach Alfred Johansson. But doing so minus some of the key men who remain from last term would significantly heighten the challenge he faces.
