articles.title: Everything Luke Fickell said ahead of Week 1 vs. Notre Dame
articles.summary: The Badgers head coach had a lot to say ahead of Wisconsin’s season opener.
articles.body:
The Wisconsin Badgers are in action for the first time this weekend as they take on the Notre Dame Fighting Irish on primetime on Sunday evening, just ahead of Labor Day.

It'll be one of the most difficult challenges on paper of Luke Fickell's tenure, as the Badgers are facing a top-five team in the country. Wisconsin is currently a 20.5-point underdog, with the over/under at 47.5 points.

Ahead of the game, head coach Luke Fickell spoke with the media on Monday, breaking down the matchup, sharing key injury news, looking ahead to the season, and answering key questions.

Here's everything Fickell said in his weekly presser ahead of Week 1 against Notre Dame.

Welcome back. Here we go again. So another year, another start. I think this is obviously, first games are always unique, right? I mean, this is obviously a different one and a unique one. But I think that you'll ask plenty of questions about where you are and the things that you have. And, you know, everybody talks about what's your identity? And I think that's what the start of a new year is always about. I think, the last few years in particular, I think the identities of a lot of teams, I think, are what you look for in Game 1. We all have the idea of what our program is and what we put up on walls and things we talk about.

But there's so much different each and every year, even in a sense of trying to compare yourself to the rest of the people in the league. I stopped doing it after, in particular last year, because you have no idea. So the idea of focusing on us and the things that we got to be able to do, I think, is what is most important. I think we had a really good camp. I wasn't kidding when I said that I thought we were in a good place when I was at Big Ten Media Day. I think it's continued to grow throughout the entire camp. We did some things a little bit different this fall camp, meaning that we, just structure-wise, in the first 10 days we went really hard and pretty normal to what we did. We kind of shifted gears a little bit in that, you know, that midweek for about 8 days. We basically got into version of what we would say some version of game week. And I hope it kept us healthier and put us in a better place as we get rolling here in the fall.

We have a lot of unknowns. I think that's the beauty of it, right? I mean, we got a new quarterback that we feel really good about. I'm sure you'll ask questions about him. But we also have never seen him truly play a game and looked in the eyes of those things. And so that's what I think us as coaches, what continues to drive us and motivate us, but also keep us up at night. And so excited about getting to the 6th, that's for sure. It's a longer week, this unique week. Game 1s are always that way, but in particular playing on a Sunday where there's 7 games in Week 0. Obviously, majority of the games on a Friday and Saturday, and then you play on Sunday.

So there's a lot of things that, most importantly, we've got to be able to handle, and it's more mental than anything else. That doesn't mean we're ready. Doesn't mean that the hay's in the barn of any sorts. We're just getting into game week practice. But now it's about handling the emotions of a lot of things, the mental side of a lot of things, a lot of the unknowns, and staying within ourselves. And so that's where more than anything else, I would say that the leadership has done a really good job, and I think that we'll do a better job as we continue through this week.

On Emerson Mandell and Kevin Heywood's status for Week 1…

That's why I said there's a lot of unknowns because we don't know. And there's still, there's still some time for us. Those guys have been back in some capacity, but I couldn't tell you exactly where we are to date right now. And so that'll be a little bit closer towards a game time decision. Both of them took some reps today. And as far as a lot of guys took reps today.

But that's the one spot probably on the offensive line that this week is going to be a lot of determining factors. I think this is where we have to be smart in all the things that we're doing. And we know this is a huge game in Game 1 and kicking off the way we're kicking off in Lambeau against Notre Dame. But we also understand there's a journey here. And so, you know, there's a part of this thing that we've got to make sure that as we get closer towards game time, we do the things that are going to be best for us for this entire journey. And so there aren't decisions made completely on a lot of guys just yet. And we'll have to figure that out as we get closer to game day.

On Marcus Freeman's success as a head coach and if anything has surprised Fickell…

No, I think that, like I said, I've known him for a long time and been around some really good coaches, and I think that when those guys kind of go off on their own, I think the unique thing is they find their way to create the things that make them even better. And so, no, I think that, you know, seeing the growth of that program and team from afar, there's a part of it that makes you happy about it.

Having a history with not just him, but a lot of the guys that are there with that staff. But that's not surprising to me at all. And I think that's, for whatever reason, I think the unique thing is guys find a way to create their own identities and a lot of different things. And I think the ones that have the most success, like Marcus has, are ones that create the identity for themselves, not just where they've been, whether it's when he was with us in Cincinnati or his time at Ohio State or his time under Jim Tressel. I think that the really good ones find a way to create an identity for themselves. And I think that's what they've done a great job of.

No, no. I think that right now those guys are all taking reps. Obviously, Colton's taking the reps with the ones. I think today we still continue to have both those guys rep with the twos. That's another one of those things. I don't know that we'll ever designate a whole lot of who is the No. 2.

We've all seen this in the past. I think the opportunities are still going to be there for those guys to compete on a daily basis. We want to give both those guys opportunities and be ready. The nice thing is it's not like we've had in the past where truly you're switching some versions of what guys can do based on who's in there with the ones and with the twos and even with the third group or who's rolling in there on the 1Bs or 2Bs. So those guys have been able to be able to continue to do the same things. And I think that gives them the chance to grow. And if we get to that point and we got to make some of those decisions, we'll have to make it.

On what it means for local kids to be playing at Lambeau…

No, I think there's so much more. I think when you get to game day, I think when you pull up there, I'm sure those guys, there'll be some emotions. But I think the magnitude of the game, I think the magnitude of where we are as a program and a team. I think these guys all in this program, whether it's their first year here or a guy like Aaron Witt's 6th year here, there's a lot riding not just on this week but on all the things that we're doing. And so I've tried to counterbalance that in a lot of ways. I'm not trying to make this about anything more than what it is.

I'm not making this thing about anything more than, there's a rivalry or there's some storylines of some sorts like that. There's enough on the plates, and whether they're from Green Bay or we've got guys that they're in their first year here, I think everybody understands and recognizes maybe that there's a little different pressure in the world today, and in particular for us.

And so I don't know that the magnitude of even where we're going to be at right now has had nearly as much to do [with it]. Now we get there on Sunday, I think that there'll be a little bit of something different. The lights come on. I think that's a good point. Obviously, there'll be some things to manage, but that's not something I think [about], because of all the other things we have to worry about throughout the entire week.

On how Colton Joseph's experience will help him slow down…

Well, that's what I said from the get-go. Like, he's played a lot of games, he played a lot of big games. I mean, at quarterback, everybody understands there's a lot of pressure on guys no matter where you are, I say that for us is because I haven't looked him in the eyes in those games. That doesn't mean that he worries about, I wonder what coaches are going to think about me, or what this, that, or the other thing in the game. Like, so to me, I don't know that it's going to be something that all of a sudden is going to be overwhelming to Colton.

That whole idea of, hey, as the lights turn on, you're in Lambeau Field. Yeah, I think there'll be a magnitude of those things, but I think that Colton has done a really good job. I think what he's done even a better job after spring football and through fall camp is recognizing the people that he has around him. And we all put a lot of pressure on the quarterback, and we all understand that the quarterback position is where everything starts, in particular on the offense, but even within your team and your program.

And I think having some balance to some of the things we've been able to do, some of the guys around him to be able to shoulder some of the leadership as a team and even as an offense, has taken some of that off of his shoulders. And so I want nothing more for Colton to relax, be the ball player that he is, recognize that, yeah, maybe he hasn't been in Lambeau Field, and maybe he hasn't been on, so to speak, national television. But, you know, once the ball's kicked off, there's not that much difference. The speed of the game is the speed of the game, and he'll be able to adjust to that.

On what he's looking for from the offense in Week 1…

I think there's a balance. I think more than anything offensively, we've got to make sure we've got balance in what we're doing. Colton's got to be able to have balance as well. He's got to be able to let people around him do things. He's got to be able to be aggressive and do the things he needs to do. At the quarterback position in particular, it comes down to decision-making. I mean, it's knowing your strengths and playing to them. And so all Game 1s, I don't care who it is, it could be CJ Carr on the other side, there's a lot of similarities in what you expect from a quarterback in Game 1.

I mean, nobody's hit a quarterback since they played last year. So your ability to take care of the football, and that doesn't just mean not throwing it into coverage and throwing it like Your ability to take care of the football, your ability to make good decisions, your ability to be able to handle the situations that arise. Every quarterback is going to have to go through that, in particular on Game 1, because, you know, no one's going to put their quarterbacks live in this day and age. And so I think for me, for him, I think that's the biggest thing is just reminding him that the game that he's played in a lot of them, there'll be some adjustments maybe just with the nature of the speed of the game. But it's all about decision-making. It's all about making sure you trust and believe in the people that are around you, and you take what is there.

On challenge/benefit of facing Notre Dame defense in Week 1…

Well, I don't know if we want to answer that question. The truth, you would love obviously to have a preseason game like we've all talked about. Get your feet wet, recognize where you are. That's not always the case. And so we don't get those choices. So in some ways, we've kind of looked at, hey, this is no better way than what we've talked about. We've got to find a way to close a gap. Well, we're going to find out where we are in closing that gap. If they're really the No. 1 team or the No. 2 team or No. 3 team in the country or the odds-on favorite to be the national champ, whatever. I mean, we're going to find out real quick at what gaps there were and what we've seen and where we are.

And that doesn't mean that, um, there has to be a giant gap, and then there's different ways of closing those gaps. But I think it also is, you put us in perspective to say, hey, knowing what we need to be able to do coming out of fall camp. And in the long run, I think it's going to help us, you know. I think it's really going to help us. I think it helped us adjust some of the things we needed to do for fall camp to make sure we came out in a different frame of mind, in a different place physically, as we enter into Game 1.

On if they played live reps in practice…

No, I'm gonna be honest with you. We did in spring. We did a couple snaps early in fall camp. But to be honest with you, the plan was, hey, we're probably not going to do a ton of live ball as we get closer. Yeah, it'd be nice to have, you know, a version of playing Week 0. Um, but that's not the case. And so we're going to get to find out a lot about ourselves, get to measure ourselves really quick to find out how much this gap is closed.

On whether they'll avoid Leonard Moore in secondary…

I mean, again, we've got to not just think that we can't go that direction. Like, I'm not saying he's not the best in the country. I'm not saying he's not a top 2, 3 pick in the country. But the idea is you still got to be able to run your offense. And I think the thing that I love about what it is that we do is we make people do everything. And, so, he'll have a chance to prove that he's the best in the country, not just in the way he covers but also in the way that he maybe sets some edges and maybe the way that he has to fit in on some ability to tackles and things like that.

So, I think again that's a part of being smart, but that's also a part of saying, hey, look, Game 1, man, we've got to be able to run our offense. Tthis is a challenge not only to the entire offense, it's a challenge to the wideouts. I mean, everybody's got the goal and the dream to play at the next level. Well, I tell you what, you're going to go out there and you're going to face not just in particular there at the corner position, but you're going to face a lot of NFL players.

And there's no better way for us to measure ourselves individually against the best or, again, closing that gap as it is as a team. And so, I think that there's a part of being smart, but there's also a part of challenging ourselves. And there's some adjustments that will have to be made throughout the entire game. But I'm interested to see how that matchup continues to go and how our guys take the challenge and run with it.

On challenge of defending CJ Carr, his growth…

Yeah, I mean, I think there's a lot of new weapons. I think that there's obviously some guys back that he's really comfortable with. There are some new tight ends, but, I think most importantly, receiver-wise, there are some guys that maybe played 2 years ago that maybe has a connection with. They didn't play a lot that year, but we know they've got a very incredible amount of talent. Sometimes that's even more difficult because you've got to spread the ball around so much.

But, what I would say is his best is his ability to manage a game, his ability to move the ball. He doesn't make a ton of mistakes, but the mistakes he did make, even as a— I don't even know if I call them redshirt freshmen anymore— a freshman, as a second-year guy last year, it didn't seem like it cost him the next series or anything like that. And so I would guess he's very mature beyond his years.

So I think the balance that the offense has, I think is where his strength is. Does he throw a great deep ball? Yeah. But I think his timing on things is where, as a younger guy last year, I thought he was very different. And so, we'll see where he's grown to. We'll see where their offense has grown to. I know them in general. I know Coach Denbrock in a lot of ways, and they're not gonna get away from the run just because they've got a Heisman-hopeful quarterback and maybe some new tailbacks. The balance of their offense will be what's really important. But I'm sure they'll feature him in a lot of different ways, and we'll see how he's grown.

On the value of previous tape for Game 1 prep…

Well, again, I think that the retention of their staff too tells you where they are. And yes, they have a lot of players returning. I think that's where the unique thing in college football is today. I mean, I said it at the opening that it's hard to compare yourself against a lot of people in the country because, A) you don't know exactly where you are with the nature of 35, 40, 50 new guys on your team, but you don't know where everybody else is. I.e., that's not always the case for the top 5 teams in the country, top 10 teams in the country. And Notre Dame is one of those.

I mean, that's why I say closing the gap and recognizing where you are against the very best. They've added a lot of pieces, but I think that obviously the core nucleus and the crux of their team and their program was there last year and has been guys they've developed from within. And so it does give you an idea of what you're going to be playing against. But I think that more than anything, I think that's where the toughest thing about not just Game 1 but college football is today. And, you know, you make some of those mistakes, and I think maybe I've made some of those mistakes in the past couple years, spending time thinking about where you are based on your league and based on the games that you play, when in reality, as you start the thing, you have no idea.

And so to focus too much on them is not where we wanted to be. But it makes it a little bit easier when they've got the retention that they've had, both as players and coaches. As far as their defensive front goes, what makes going against that group a challenge? Well, they're aggressive, but I think, in the back end of things, they're going to get on you. And they've been a man-coverage team in a lot of ways, and they'll mix it up some. But I'm sure the philosophy is to give up nothing easy. And I think that's what can wear on teams. I mean, you watch them play against USC last year, and USC makes some plays, and it's a pretty competitive first half in particular. But they didn't change a ton. They came out the second half, continued to put the pressure on them, continue to get on receivers, and make it very, very, very challenging for you to take anything easy. And I think that gives them the opportunity up front to be aggressive.

And so I think maybe, from what they had last year to what they have this year in particular up front on the defensive line, and I think they're going to have more depth, I think they're going to have more length, I think they may have some even more NFL true players up front on the defensive line. And so there's no doubt that it'll be a challenge for us up front. Not gonna say it's going to be the best defensive front we play the entire year, but if it's not the most talented defensive front, it'll be one of the most talented defensive fronts.

On change to in-season practice schedule…

There was a lot of changes in the things that we wanted to be able to do, and [so I said], hey, let's look and figure out what's going to give us a better chance to be successful. But you visit with some of your guys, you spend some time with that leadership group, and it had also been a bigger philosophy change as far as, hey, what can you do as far as school-wise? And so I didn't want to do something in the morning that was going to be rolling at 6 AM.

But I think twofold: our guys enjoying and liking the ability to do things earlier in the morning with our school being able to handle some of those things where we don't have to be off the field by 10 o'clock, so the guys can get into all the classes early. There's been a balance of us being able to do that, and it's taken some work from not just our academic people, but a lot of people. But I think it's better for us. I think the biggest change is for the coaches. They've been in a routine for so long. I have, too, in the fall, that norm and routine, I don't think is what was best for the players. So, we switched it up, and I can't tell you how we love it just yet. But I know the players do.

On comfort level and difference with rushing attack on offense…

We'll see. I mean, like I said, there's no better front, more talented front, than we'll probably see than Game 1. And so I think that there's a balance to it. I think our offensive line is one that I couldn't tell you today, right now, who's going to be up there up front to start. And there could be a combination, and I bet you will see a lot of guys play. And I'm not saying that in Week 4 that's what we want, but I think as this journey begins, we know that there's some things up front that guys have worked, guys have provided some things. They've earned the opportunity to be able to play. This isn't a tryout period. Not saying that, obviously, but I think there's going to be a combination of things that we've got to be able to do up front.

And so I think the balance of the quarterback, but also the running backs. I mean, it's not just, hey, well, the offensive front's got to do a great job at creating holes. I mean, a really good back and some dynamic backs can make it a little bit easier on the offensive line as well. And so that's where I say about the balance. The balance isn't always just, hey, you got to be 50% run and 50% pass. The balance is saying, hey, you got to have a quarterback that can make some things happen sometimes if the pressure or the front breaks down in the passing game. And you have to have some backs that, at times, if somebody's in the hole, they win one-on-ones. And so the game is not, hey, we got to design the perfect play every single time that we get you in a hole that's wide open so that we can run the football.

So that's where I mean there's a balance there. And that's another reason why I like where we are. I think we've got a group of backs that are going to give us a chance that if everything isn't perfect, they can play through imperfect, you know. And I think we've got a guy, a group of guys up front on the offensive line that, as they build their confidence, as they build their ability to play together, that they'll be able to play through imperfect a lot better than I think we have in the last couple years. And so we don't know everything, but like I said, the first one will be an incredible challenge to find out where we are with that too.

On if any true freshmen have earned right for early playing time, being on two-deep…

It's hard to remember some of these guys. They come in early, so it's hard to say who's even a true freshman. I know this, that a guy that didn't come in early, [cornerback] Donovan Dunmore, you'll see out there a bit on some special teams. There's no doubt [tight end] Jack Sievers is a guy that you'll see out there on some special teams.

I don't want to leave out a bunch of others, and I can't think sometimes off the top of my head all the guys that are true freshmen or came in in January. Those 2 guys, for sure, stand out to me that will have definite roles on September 6th. And there's another one, right? I mean, like, you know, under the lights in Lambeau Field that an 18-year-old that's going to be something we got to find out a lot about ourselves as well.

On a favorite memory, story with Marcus Freeman…

No, no, the most important thing for us is that we keep ourselves focused on the things that matter. And what matters is when that ball's kicked off, where we are. And, if at some point in time it becomes a bigger deal, then it takes the pressure off our players and our team; great, we'll get into it. But, for us and for the things we got to be able to, we know what this is all about. And so, when that comes up, I'll defer and basically, in general saying it's not just Coach Freeman, it's not just Marcus that we got a long history with.

There's a lot of guys over there that, in particular, we got great relationships with and had great relationships with. And like I've always said, I wouldn't be sitting here today if it wasn't for not just him but a lot of those guys over on that, uh, in that staff. But we all know that I'm not the greatest in particular of keeping great relationships, in particular on game days. Whether that was my brother on the other side of the fence or not, it'll be cordial in the way that we go about things. And there's a game to be played. And so whether that's before we talk about things in the press conference, on the field before the game, there's something that's special about game day, and we'll keep it that way.

On the mindset of having no Plan B this year…

Yeah, I mean, as you go into games, there's adjustments in being able to adapt, but the idea of no Plan B is, guys, like, we got to put it all out there. And the whole philosophy and motto of let it fly is important, and guys got to understand that. And I think they have. I think that they recognize that. And part of that, like I've said, is trying to back off a little bit in the idea of how much pressure is on all of us to perform. It is what it is. I mean, this is the game today.

But the idea of, hey, let's not have any excuses. Let's not have anything that we're holding on to from the past. Let's make sure everything we do as we're moving forward— there's a lot of guys, a lot of different histories, whether it's history with guys on the other side of the ball in Game 1 or histories from other schools they've been at. The idea is, guys, we've got 9 months, 8 months together here for us to do some things and to set some standards and to create our own history. And let's not worry about a lot of the other things that we have no control over. And so that's a part of what that— hey, no plan Bs, man. Let's not worry about the alternatives, and let's just make sure we understand we'll continue to move forward.

On status of RBs Bryan Jackson, Nate Palmer, and thoughts on new availability report rules…

No, I mean, we could just list everybody as doubtful, probable. I don't take a whole lot into that. I understand what it is and why it is, and it's not like we're trying to play any games, but that's why even like today, I can't tell you exactly. The guys are back out there practicing, but you're talking about game 1, and how much are they? I don't know. Those are new guys that haven't played, haven't played here with us. But they'll be up, they'll be practicing.

How many guys can play at the tailback position? I think that's probably a bigger thing. I mean, like, you can't really think you're going to play 4 guys. I mean, if you're gonna have some consistency in the things you're going to do, you've got to be able to roll with a couple guys. And so it has been a little bit more difficult because that room has had some nagging injuries and miss some of fall camp. But there's some things we're gonna have to figure out this week. And as we go into game 1, you know, that plan being in place as to who's going to be the guy that's going to be 1A and 1B. And then if we get to another situation, then obviously we'll be able to use some other guys. But, I think there's still some things within that room that we got to be able to see this week. I can tell you this: Abu Sama is our 1A. And from there, I think there's a lot of things that we'll have to figure out as we continue to move forward.

On balancing how to use Colton Joseph's dual threat ability with staying healthy

Well, I think that's a part of making good decisions. The whole idea is there's no plan B. We're not trying to save things. Like, we've got to be aggressive. We've got to be able to do the things we need to be able to do. It's not second-guessing and things like that. So, there's a good plan. And his ability doesn't have to just be running the football. It can be ability to just create more time. It's also, hopefully, it can slow down some people on the other side, as far as even their pass rush.

There's a balance to the quarterback's abilities to move in the pocket and create things if he has to run that you got to think about as a defense in the way that which you rush. And that can help an offensive line too. And so, there's a part of, as you get into the game, recognizing how people want to play and how they're going to play you based on the abilities that maybe just your quarterback has, maybe the abilities that your running back has, and as we all know, the abilities that your wide receivers have. So, that's where everybody hears me say balance, and you keep saying balance. Well, it's not 50% run, 50% pass. The balance is understanding and recognizing the abilities that we have and how people have to play you and how that can be used to your advantage as well.

articles.title: Who are the Raiders’ all-time INT and passes defensed leaders?
articles.summary: Two Hall of Famers own the Raiders’ all-time interceptions and passes defensed records.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders have a long list of defensive stars that have represented the franchise throughout its storied history.

Raiders great Charles Woodson was one of the top safeties of his era, while Vann McElroy helped the team win the Super Bowl at the end of the 1983 season. The Raiders' defensive stalwarts got their hands on many interceptions and deflections throughout their tenures with the team, and the franchise's leaderboards in those departments are filled with elite performers who played sensationally in the secondary.

Let's take a look at who the Raiders' all-time interceptions leaders, and leaders in passes defensed are.

Who ranks in the top five all-time in interceptions for the Raiders?

Willie Brown and Lester Hayes are tied for the most interceptions in Raiders franchise history with 39, ranking T-No. 1 overall.

Brown, a Pro Football Hall of Famer, recorded four or more interceptions five times across the 12 seasons that he played with the Raiders from 1967-78. Hayes led the NFL in interceptions in 1980 with 13 as a member of the Raiders.

Terry McDaniel (34 INT) ranks No. 3 overall behind Brian and Hayes, followed by Vann McElroy (31 INT), who ranks No. 4, and George Atkinson and Jack Tatum (30 INT), who rank T-No. 5 all-time.

Who ranks in the top five all-time in passes defensed for the Raiders?

Charles Woodson (84), Nnamdi Asomugha (61), Michael Huff (53) and Stanford Routt (51) rank Nos. 2-4 on the Raiders' all-time passes defensed list, with Chris Johnson and David Amerson (45) ranking T-No. 5.

Which current Raiders player ranks highest on the franchise's all-time interceptions and passes defensed lists?

Isaiah Pola-Mao is the current Raiders star who ranks highest on the team's all-time interceptions list. Pola-Mao currently has three interceptions to his name with the Raiders, which ranks No. 89 on the list.

Maxx Crosby is also the current team leader in passes defensed with 29, which ranks T-No. 10 in Raiders history.

articles.title: Manchester City Reportedly Reaches Deal With Chelsea For Enzo Fernández
articles.summary: Manchester City has reportedly struck a deal with Chelsea to sign midfielder and Argentinian champion Enzo Fernández.
articles.body: Enzo Fernández is about to make a one-way trip across England. Manchester City has reached a deal with Chelsea to sign the 25-year-old midfielder, The Athletic reported on Tuesday morning. Fernández has reportedly been given permission by Chelsea to undergo a medical, with his transfer costing Manchester City €125 million ($169 million) — which ties the Premier League transfer record that's also held by Alexander Isak (Newcastle United to Liverpool in 2025). Fernández originally joined Chelsea in January 2023 on a €106.8 million transfer fee ($125 million) from Benfica. Fernández recently commenced his fifth season with Chelsea. Last season (2025-26), he logged a career-high 10 goals and four assists. He previously played one season with Benfica in Primeira Liga (2022-23), which was preceded by three seasons with River Plate in Liga Argentina (2018-19, 2021 and 2022). Meanwhile, Fernández just wrapped up playing for Argentina in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, knocking through two scores over seven contests in the tournament. Fernández also played for Argentina in its 2022 World Cup triumph. On the Argentina front, superstar striker Lionel Messi announced his retirement from the national team on Monday. Both Manchester City and Chelsea are 2-0-0 in the 2026-27 Premier League season. Man. City will host Chelsea on Dec. 12 and play them on the road on April 24.

articles.title: Leeds United eyeing a move for Jean-Matteo Bahoya
articles.summary: Daniel Farke is at Elland Road with the Whites. Leeds United are exploring a late move for Eintracht Frankfurt winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya, according to Ben Ja...
articles.body:
Daniel Farke is at Elland Road with the Whites. Leeds United are exploring a late move for Eintracht Frankfurt winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya, according to Ben Jacobs .

The 21-year-old has emerged as a target for the Leeds hierarchy following an unpredictable few days in the transfer market.

Leeds' interest comes after the explosive winger turned down a move to Hull City.

Hull had reached an agreement with Eintracht Frankfurt, but Bahoya rejected the proposed switch to the MKM Stadium, keeping his options open late in the window.

Sunderland have also monitored Bahoya's situation as they consider alternative wide options.

Leeds have now stepped up internal discussions to assess whether they can complete a deal before the deadline, viewing the French winger as an ideal option to add attacking firepower.

Bahoya came through the Angers youth system in France before moving to Eintracht Frankfurt, where he has built a reputation as one of the Bundesliga's most exciting young wide players.

Bahoya can play across the frontline, but is most effective on the left, cutting inside onto his stronger foot.

Leeds' renewed interest follows their failure to land Mykhailo Mudryk, who is set to join Tottenham Hotspur.

With five signings already secured, the Whites have been active in the market as they look to consolidate their Premier League status.

Farke's side have started the 2026/27 campaign brightly, picking up four points from two league matches and progressing to the EFL Cup third round.

Leeds travel to the AMEX Stadium on Saturday to face Brighton & Hove Albion, after which a cup tie against Chelsea awaits.

articles.title: Liverpool send Harvey Elliott to Valencia on loan
articles.summary: Harvey Elliott has joined Valencia on loan from Liverpool for the remainder of the 2026/27 season.The 23-year-old midfielder completed his move to the La Lig...
articles.body:
Harvey Elliott has joined Valencia on loan from Liverpool for the remainder of the 2026/27 season.

The 23-year-old midfielder completed his move to the La Liga side before the summer transfer deadline, with the deal containing no option or obligation to make the transfer permanent.

Elliott joined Liverpool from Fulham in 2019 and has gone on to make 149 appearances for the club, scoring 15 goals. He has also collected a number of major honours, including two Premier League titles, the UEFA Super Cup, FIFA Club World Cup, League Cup and FA Cup.

The England Under-21 international spent last season on loan at Aston Villa before returning to Anfield in the summer. However, he struggled to establish himself in new manager Andoni Iraola's plans and was left out of the squad for Liverpool's recent league fixtures against Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest.

Elliott will now look to reignite his career in Spain, with Valencia currently 16th in La Liga after failing to win any of their opening three matches.

articles.title: Salford confirm Scarr and Asiimwe signings
articles.summary: Salford City confirm the signings of Dan Scarr from Wrexham and Nathan Asiimwe on loan from Charlton Athletic.
articles.body:
Salford City have confirmed the signing of defender Dan Scarr from Wrexham and completed a season-long loan deal for Nathan Asiimwe from Charlton Athletic.

The club say the 31-year-old Scarr has signed a "multi-year" deal at the AIG Stadium and joins for an undisclosed fee.

Scarr, who has won promotion with Wycombe Wanderers, Plymouth Argyle and Wrexham, leaves the Racecourse Ground after two years in north Wales.

"I'm really looking forward to getting stuck into it," he told the club's website. "From speaking to the manager, the owners, I know where they want to go and I feel like that aligns with the ambitions and the moments I want to create in my career so I'm really looking forward to it.

"When you look back, they're the moments you always remember and it gives you goosebumps looking back to those times.

"I've learnt that from every team I've been in and I've picked up little bits at every team I've been successful at. That's what's sculpted me into what I am now and hopefully I can bring some of those qualities here and push on."

Asiimwe has already had loan spells with Hartlepool United, Walsall and AFC Wimbledon, with the 21-year-old making 42 appearances for the Dons last season.

"I've had to be patient but now I'm here I'm buzzing to get going, excited to be involved in what the plans are for the future," the right-back told the Salford website.

"I'd describe myself as hard-working, I'll give my all for the badge, get up and down the wings. I like to one-v-one defend and help out in both boxes. When I get in the final third I try and take my man on, get my cross in, get some assists and try to get a goal or two.

"For me it's more than just development, I'm looking further than that and hopefully, if I can help the team achieve its goal this season, who knows what the future can bring."

articles.title: Countdown to Kickoff: Chris Olave is the Saints Player of Day 12
articles.summary: Fresh off his best season and a lucrative contract extension, Chris Olave will be a vital part of the New Orleans Saints' success in 2026.
articles.body:
Just 12 days separate us from the New Orleans Saints regular season opener. The Saints travel north to start 2026, playing at the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Sept. 13. Wearing No. 12 for New Orleans is star Chris Olave at wide receiver. Olave is coming off his best season and a lucrative contract extension. He'll be a major part of the Saints offense. He's also the most recent in our Saints Player of the Day series.

Drafted: Round 1, 11th overall in 2022 (Saints)

After an explosive senior year of 93 catches, 1,764 yards, and 26 touchdowns at Mission Hills High School, Olave joined "The" Ohio State University. Even with the Buckeyes incredible depth at wide receiver, Olave managed to catch 12 balls for 197 yards as a true freshman in 2018, including two scores and a blocked punt against bitter rival Michigan. Olave was a huge part of the Buckeyes attack in 2019, catching 49 passes for a team-high 849 yards and leading the Big Ten with 12 touchdown catches. He'd lead Ohio State in all three receiving categories during a Covid-shortened 2020 season with 50 catches, 729 yards, and 7 scores. Olave capped off his Buckeyes career in 2021 by leading the Big Ten with 13 scoring receptions, pulling in 65 receptions for 936 yards. A two-time First Team All-Big Ten selection, Olave left as Ohio State's all-time leader in touchdown receptions (35) and third in both catches and receiving yards.

With their first of two first round choices in the 2022 NFL draft, the Saints took Olave with the 11th overall pick. He was the third receiver selected after Drake London and Ohio State teammate Garrett Wilson. Olave had immediate success as a rookie, leading the Saints with 72 receptions and 1,042 yards while scoring 4 times. His encore performance in 2023 was even better, as he pulled in 87 passes for 1,123 yards and 5 touchdowns. In the process, Olave became only the fourth player in franchise history to have back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons in his first two years with New Orleans. Unfortunately, he was unable to make it three straight. Olave got 2024 off to a strong start with 31 receptions and 387 yards in his first seven games. However, the second of two concussions in Week 9 would shelve him for the rest of the season.

Olave's football durability and long-term health were both a major concern heading into the 2025 campaign. He responded with his best and most durable season, missing only the season finale and playing a career-best 884 snaps. Olave was targeted 156 times, pulling in 100 receptions for 1,163 yards and 9 touchdowns. All were the best numbers of his four-year career, as only Michael Thomas had more catches in a single season. What perhaps was most impressive is that Olave continued to be productive even when at times he and Juwan Johnson were the only viable receiving weapons.

New Orleans locked up Chris Olave with a lucrative four-year contract extension this offseason. The Saints also added more weaponry at receiver and running back. However, Olave should still be the top weapon. In 2025, he showed that he could handle the workload of a featured wideout.

articles.title: Purdue football names 6 captains for 2026 season

WEST LAFAYETTE — A season ago, Jude McCoskey was a seldom-used transfer, available in Purdue football 's jumbo package offensive set.

McCoskey, Purdue's projected starting right tackle, joins receiver De'Nylon Morrissette and quarterback Ryan Browne , a captain for the second straight season , as leaders of the offense.

They join defensive captains linebacker Charles Correa , cornerback Hudauri Hines, and defensive tackle Curt Neal, a transfer from Illinois. Correa and Hines are returning starters. Correa's 96 tackles last season are the most among Purdue returnees.

AFC Wimbledon have signed goalkeeper Joe Bursik from Championship side Portsmouth, and defender Freddie Simmonds from Premier League side Brighton, both on loan for the rest of the season.

Bursik, 26, returns to the club, where he joined the academy as an eight-year-old before leaving for Stoke City aged 16.

He kept seven clean sheets in 16 Championship games for the Potters in 2020-21 before going on loan to Telford, Accrington, Doncaster and Peterborough.

Simmonds, 18, has yet to play a first-team game for Brighton, having been with the Seagulls since the age of six.

articles.title: Dodgers Activate Will Smith, Justin Wrobleski And Dalton Rushing From IL
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers activated catchers Will Smith and Dalton Rushing and left-hander Justin Wrobleski from the injured list.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Dodgers are slowly getting back to full strength. The Dodgers announced on Tuesday afternoon that they've activated catchers Will Smith and Dalton Rushing and left-hander Justin Wrobleski from the injured list. They also added infielder Alex Freeland to the MLB roster. To make room on the roster for the aforementioned returnees, the Dodgers sent outfielder Alek Thomas and catcher Ben Rortvedt — whom they acquired from the New York Mets before the MLB trade deadline — to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Smith, an All-Star in each of the last three complete seasons (2023-25), hasn't played for the Dodgers since June 5 due to a neck injury. Over the 52 games Smith has appeared in this season, he has totaled six home runs, 23 RBIs and a 101 OPS+, while sporting a .249/.338/.382 slash line. Rushing, who took Smith's place as the team's everyday catcher in the wake of his neck injury, hasn't played since Aug. 1 due to an arm injury. Across 74 games, Rushing has logged 12 home runs, 36 RBIs, a 123 OPS+ and 1.4 wins above replacement, while possessing a .253/.335/.475 slash line. Wrobleski hasn't made a start for the Dodgers since Aug. 15, as he dealt with a forearm injury. The left-hander was an All-Star this year and boasted a 2.62 ERA entering his July 28 outing before posting a combined 8.69 ERA over his ensuing four starts, with a stint on the 15-day injured list following. In all, Wrobleski has recorded a 3.56 ERA, a 1.10 WHIP, a 114 ERA+ and two wins above replacement across 126 ⅓ innings pitched (20 starts/21 appearances). The Dodgers could soon have their full starting rotation. Fellow left-hander Blake Snell is four starts back from elbow surgery, and right-hander Tyler Glasnow was activated last week after back spasms kept him off the mound for manager Dave Roberts for roughly 15 weeks. The next piece in the puzzle for the Dodgers' rotation could be Shohei Ohtani, as the two-way superstar hasn't pitched since July 3 due to knee inflammation and is also dealing with a biceps issue. Granted, Ohtani has continued to be the team's primary designated hitter. Los Angeles is the No. 2 seed in the National League at 82-55, good for a half-game lead on the Atlanta Braves (82-56) for the second wild-card round bye and good for being 2.5 games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (85-53) for the best record in the NL. The Dodgers also hold a 9.5-game lead on the San Diego Padres (73-65) for first place in the NL West. Los Angeles opens a three-game series at home against the St. Louis Cardinals on Tuesday night.

articles.title: Bear Bachmeier and Jeremy Lin talk faith and ‘playing for so much more’
articles.summary: Bachmeier’s latest interview left him feeling "starstruck" as he bonded with Jeremy Lin over their similar religious beliefs and representing Asian Americans...
articles.body:
Bear Bachmeier 's latest interview left him feeling "starstruck."

BYU's first Asian American starting quarterback and Jeremy Lin, the NBA's first player of Chinese or Taiwanese descent, interviewed each other in a new AMAZN HQ video . Bachmeier admitted he grew up inspired by Lin, especially after he waved off Kobe Bryant before nailing a 3-pointer in 2014.

"After that moment I was like, I just want to be like Jeremy Lin," Bachmeier said. "Unfortunately, I'm not a great basketball player, but (I) found a different avenue."

In the 15-minute video shared on YouTube on Monday, Bachmeier and Lin discussed a variety of topics — from their faith to their Asian American heritage.

Lin, a Christian, asked Bachmeier, a Catholic, about the role faith plays in his life. Bachmeier pointed to his journey to BYU.

"I'm a big believer in everything happens for a reason," he said. "Coming out of high school, I committed to Stanford, and I was at Stanford for four months. My coach ended up getting fired, and I felt some kind of calling to leave Stanford and go to a different place where there's more stability."

Bachmeier described leaving Stanford for BYU as "the hardest decision I ever had to make." But it paid off.

At BYU, he became the program's first true freshman to start a season opener, and he went on to lead BYU to its first Big 12 Championship appearance.

"I'm just such a better person, and I'm such a better player being at BYU. So faith is very, very important to me and has played a big role for me," he said.

Lin said he could see the hope Bachmeier's faith brings him, which is something Lin has experienced with his own faith.

"A huge point on Christianity is just you have hope," Lin said. "You have hope that things happen for a reason. You have hope that the end will play out a certain way. You have hope that God never leaves you, that he never forsakes you. There's just so many things that provide hope and positivity. And so the lens that you view the whole world is one of that, and I can feel that even just in a short conversation."

Bachmeier shared how he leaned on hope and his faith in God while his sister was hospitalized and his dad had a brain tumor.

"The only thing you can really do at that point is pray and just ask God for miracles and miracles are true," he said. "Anyways, they're doing really well, and it's just — you got to have faith. You got to have hope."

Bear Bachmeier and Jeremy Lin on representing Asian Americans

Bachmeier wasn't immune to Asian American stereotypes as a kid.

"Growing up, all my friends joked around, just like, 'Oh, he's probably good at math,' and I was kind of good at math," he said. "But I feel like there's just so much more I wanted to show of myself, and especially from a sports side."

He said that the platform and leadership responsibilities that come with being BYU's starting quarterback "breaks that barrier of Asians kind of just being shy and being in the corner."

"It just meant a lot to represent such an important position and one that's so underrepresented by Asian Americans, and it means a lot," Bachmeier said. "It's always in the back of my head, like I am playing for so much. You always kind of have that initial like, 'Oh, I'm just kind of playing for myself.' But no, you're playing for so much more."

Bachmeier said kids "that look like me" come up to him and tell him that he's their hero.

"It warms my heart," he said. " … I can't believe I'm an inspiration to these kids. I'm sure you have kind of the same similarities. But it just means so much, and you're fighting for something way bigger."

Bear Bachmeier on building camaraderie with BYU teammates

When it comes to building relationships with teammates, Bachmeier said the key is actually what happens off the field.

"I think that the best camaraderie is not built on the field, but it's built off the field — going to watch a movie or going to get food, being kids, being free," he said.

He also likes to take care of his offensive linemen, which he said means "emptying my pockets when we go to eat."

Bachmeier added that the service-oriented mindset that comes from BYU's mission statements has also helped in the building of that brotherhood.

"When you're in between the lines and I'm looking at the 10 other guys who just love being great people and love serving others, that brotherhood and that bond, it just makes us such a better team," he said.

Bachmeier and BYU play their first game of the 2026 season on Saturday against Utah Tech at 6 p.m. MDT, and they plan to build on last season's success.

"Coming up on my second year at BYU and we're trying to do even better," Bachmeier said. "You never want to get complacent. You always want to be better than the year before, and (we) got a really good team."

articles.title: George Pickens Defends His Route Tempo as Criticism Over His Effort Grows
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens has faced scrutiny when his routes appear less than full speed. Some observers have interpreted those moments...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens has faced scrutiny when his routes appear less than full speed. Some observers have interpreted those moments as a lack of effort

However, Pickens has responded to criticism over his effort, explaining that fans do not always understand what a receiver's route is designed to accomplish. Here's his side of the story.

Pickens Explains Why Every Route Isn't Full Speed

Pickens said certain routes require receivers to change their speed to maintain timing with the quarterback. He also pointed to defensive schemes as another reason a route may not look as explosive as expected. NFL insider Josh Chambers shares perspectives during the gaffer's interview with sports news platform, Bleacher Report.

"Every route ain't ran at 100%. Some routes are ran at certain tempos and times just for you to have timing with the quarterback." "Some defenses are playing zone. So that was really all I was saying. You've got to kind of look at the film of the game before you critique." "If you definitely know the game, then… If you don't know the game, then I kind of see where you're coming from."

"Every route ain't ran at 100%. Some routes are ran at certain tempos and times just for you to have timing with the quarterback."

"Some defenses are playing zone. So that was really all I was saying. You've got to kind of look at the film of the game before you critique."

"If you definitely know the game, then… If you don't know the game, then I kind of see where you're coming from."

Pickens' comments come as he enters his first season with Dallas after the Cowboys acquired him from the Pittsburgh Steelers. The trade gave the Cowboys another explosive weapon alongside its existing offensive talent. Pickens has consistently shown the ability to create separation and make difficult catches, making his route-running an important part of his new role.

The Cowboys initially sent a 2026 third-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Steelers for Pickens. The Cowboys subsequently received Jones and a 2027 fourth-round pick in the later trade. On the other hand, the Steelers later acquired offensive tackle Broderick Jones from the Cowboys. The moves have created an unusual connection between the two franchises, with each team acquiring a player from the other.

Meanwhile, the Pickens deal has generated significant discussion because of his talent and potential fit in Dallas. His ability to stretch defenses could provide quarterback Dak Prescott with another dangerous option. However, expectations surrounding Pickens also mean his every movement is likely to receive considerable attention.

That scrutiny makes his explanation about route tempo particularly relevant. Receivers do not necessarily run every route at maximum speed. Depending on the concept, a player may throttle down, accelerate at a specific point, or manipulate a defender before making his break. Those details can be difficult to identify without understanding the offensive design. Pickens' message is therefore straightforward: judging a route solely by how fast it appears on television can create an incomplete picture.

The receiver wants critics to consider the film, defensive coverage, and intended timing before deciding whether a route represents poor effort. As Pickens begins his Dallas tenure, his performance will ultimately determine whether that explanation holds up under greater scrutiny. For now, he is making it clear that not every slower-looking route should be interpreted as a lack of effort. Hopefully, enough fans get his side of the story and, at least, reduce their criticisms of the athlete's performances.

articles.title: Skylar Diggins Laments Chicago Sky’s Practice Facility Delay
articles.summary: Diggins said she expects to be with the Sky next season.
articles.body:
The Chicago Sky's season hasn't gone according to plan as the team will miss the playoffs for the third year in a row.

On Tuesday, the Sky announced that marquee free agent signing Skylar Diggins would miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a knee injury that's kept her out since July 3. Hours later, Diggins held a press conference, where she shared she's been nursing the injury all season.

She also said that her "biggest frustration" of the season was not having a consistent "home base" all year, which she expected would come when she signed a two-year, $1.86 million contract with Chicago. The Sky's new $60 million practice facility was supposed to be ready by the start of the season, but was pushed back several times before the team announced in July that it would not be ready until after the season.

"I think a lot of us were promised that," Diggins said. "We thought that was going to be the case." The Sky also signed free agents Azurá Stevens and DiJonai Carrington this offseason and re-signed several others, including Rachel Banham, one of Diggins's closest friends.

The team practiced in several different locations this year, including several Chicago colleges and Wintrust Arena, where they play their home games. According to documents obtained by FOS , the Sky paid $160,000 to practice at the University of Illinois in Chicago for about a month between April and May.

Diggins, 36, said not having their own practice space affected how players could train: "Sometimes, we have limits or restrictions on how many hours we can be there, and that affects everything."

She also said new amenities will likely help the Sky with injury management; Chicago leads the league in games missed due to injury this season .

"No shade, but you know we need resources. Obviously leading the league in injuries, I think it's not coincidental," Diggins said.

Diggins expects the team to be able to use its practice facility next year, which will be located in Bedford Park, IL, a Chicagoland suburb just outside the city's southwest border. She said the team is touring the facility next week to see the progress made.

"I expect that next year, we won't lead the league in games missed to injuries," Diggins said. "And we'll be able to put together the full vision of what we wanted it to look like with all those resources."

Asked by FOS whether she would've signed with the Sky if she knew the facility would not be ready this year, Diggins said: "That's hard to say. … I understand how those things go as far as you know delays or whatever the case may be, or how it could be very nuanced as far as things that are out of your control."

Diggins started the team's first 19 games, and Chicago went 6–13. Head coach Tyler Marsh then decided to bring Diggins off the bench for their July 7 game against the Phoenix Mercury for the first time in her 11-year career. But it never happened. Diggins was ruled out before the game due to her knee injury and has not played since.

Asked whether Marsh's decision played a factor in her not playing, Diggins said it was "extremely layered," saying she had already been rehabbing her surgically repaired knee even before the season started.

But she said that there weren't any conversations with the organization about her fulfilling a bench role.

"We haven't had any conversation on that being the case," Diggins said, adding: "We've had a lot of conversations since then to reflect with both Tyler and I, [Sky GM Jeff Pagliocca] and I, the organization, [team owner] Michael Alter, and just trying to continue to work in lockstep about what this process would look like. But obviously, early in the season and now, it's been a frustrating experience for a lot of us and what we felt like the season could look like for our team versus what it turned out to be."

Diggins said she has not had any conversations about a trade elsewhere and expects to be with the Sky next year.

"I haven't expressed any desire to not talk about me in a Chicago Sky jersey next year," Diggins said.

The Sky, 15–25, have four games remaining after the FIBA World Cup break.

articles.title: Aaron Boone says it’s ‘possible’ Aaron Judge could return soon

Exactly when is unclear, but manager Aaron Boone said it's "possible" the slugging right fielder could return for the Yankees next homestand beginning Sept. 8 with the Colorado Rockies.

The Yankees host the Rockies Sept. 8-10 before hosting the rival Mets Sept. 11-13.

Judge has been sidelined since June 5 with a right rib fracture, but is with the team in California and is ramping up baseball activities. He still needs to face high-velocity pitching "during pregame workouts in Anaheim and San Diego," per MLB.com.

"He's doing well, he's here to continue to ramp up baseball activities so we're getting closer but feel good where he's at," Boone said.

Judge is on record saying he doesn't want a minor-league rehab assignment.

"I'll sign up for whenever he's ready," Yankees GM Brian Cashman told The Athletic , "and what that date happens to be is yet to be determined. I'll sign up for making sure we get him back and he's fully capable and prepared for what comes next, which is obviously going to be a grind. He's going to step into a fast-moving, fast-paced game, but he knows what he's getting into."

articles.title: Naomi Osaka Receives Special Reply From Allen Iverson After Viral US Open Tribute

articles.body:
Former NBA star Allen Iverson recently gave a special reply to Naomi Osaka's tribute to him at the U.S. Open.

Osaka opened her U.S. Open campaign on Monday with a 7-6(6), 7-6(3) win over Anastasia Zakharova. During the match, she paid tribute to Iverson by wearing a custom walkout outfit inspired by his iconic style. It featured his signature headband, cornrows, an arm sleeve and a frayed gray hoodie with newspaper clippings representing moments from her career.

She continued the tribute at her postmatch news conference, wearing an Iverson Slam Magazine cover T-shirt. Osaka also spoke about her admiration for the Basketball Hall of Famer.

"For me, he's a trailblazer. I think he's also someone that I look up to a lot, because he's kind of, like, done a lot in fashion, whether it's on purpose or not, but he's shifted the way that NBA players dress. I also think the whole conversation around clothes in sports and also just expressing yourself through style, I feel like he's someone that I look up to in that regard."

Osaka added that she had not had the opportunity to speak with Iverson but hoped he would see the interview. Her comments caught Iverson's attention, as he shared clips from the press conference on Instagram and responded:

" Wow, what a honor!! BIG FAN can't wait to meet you. @naomiosaka."

Naomi Osaka withdrew from the U.S. Open mixed doubles event due to scheduling issues. She was initially scheduled to partner with fellow Japanese player Kei Nishikori.

Naomi Osaka opened up about her outfit at the US Open first round

After defeating Anastasia Zakharova, Naomi Osaka spoke to the media during her on-court interview about her first-round win and joked that she wanted to give fans a chance to see more of her outfits as she progressed through the tournament. She then explained the inspiration behind her opening-round look.

"I just get really nervous during this the first round of this tournament because I want to do well and I want to show you guys some more outfits. So, hopefully, just hopefully I can keep playing some more matches in front of you guys," Osaka said.

"It's, I guess, my tribute to Iverson. I really like him a lot. I mean Nike said basketball. So, I said, 'OK, you want basketball? I'll give you basketball.' I love expressing myself through clothes. I don't like talking that much, I tell people. So, I'm glad you guys appreciate it, and I'll see you guys in the next round."

articles.title: When will Aaron Donald play his first game? ESPN insider shares new details
articles.summary: ESPN's Dan Graziano says a Week 1 debut is still on the table for Aaron Donald, but it's more likely he suits up in Week 2 or 3.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald returned to the practice field on Sunday afternoon for the first time since retiring after the 2023 season. Earlier in the day, he announced he was coming out of retirement to play for the Los Angeles Rams again, earning a spot on their 53-man roster.

Sean McVay has made it clear that the team will take it slow with the 35-year-old superstar, not rushing anything regarding workload or playing time. But with the start of the regular season just over a week away, Donald has to ramp things up quickly in order to be ready.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported on "NFL Live" Tuesday that Donald is more likely to make his debut in Week 2 or 3 than in the opener against the 49ers in Australia.

"Their Week 1 game is against the 49ers in Australia, and that game is nine days from today, so you can't rule anything out obviously with Aaron Donald," Graziano said. "And the Rams aren't going to rule him out in terms of playing Week 1 – at least not yet. I would say based on everything I've been told, a Week 2 or 3 debut looks more likely than Week 1. But again, it's still on the table. And in terms of workload, they'll watch his snaps. Obviously, they have a lot of depth on that defensive line, even just beyond him and Myles Garrett, so they feel they have the ability early in the season to watch his snaps and count his snaps."

McVay said there's "absolutely" a chance Donald won't play in the Rams' first game, but he "wouldn't rule anything out yet." He reiterated that the Rams are taking it a day at a time with Donald, not putting any firm timelines on his return to the field.

In his first practice on Sunday, he only did individual drills, and the Rams gave him a planned day off on Monday. He's unquestionably in terrific shape, but is he game-ready? That's what Donald and the team must figure out.

The Rams do have a roster exemption for Donald until Friday, Sept. 11, so that helps in determining whether he'll be available to play, allowing them to keep him on the 53-man roster without taking up a spot that could be used on someone else.

articles.title: Erik Sviatchenko leaving Houston Dynamo to play for Thai club Port FC
articles.summary: After four seasons in Houston, defender Erik Sviatchenko is heading to Thailand to play in that country's top division.
articles.body:
Danish defender Erik Sviatchenko is heading to Thai club Port FC following a multi-year stint with the Houston Dynamo .

Port FC play in Thailand's top division. The 34-year-old Sviatchenko first signed with the Dynamo in March 2023, playing in 80 MLS matches for Houston over the course of four seasons.

"We want to thank Erik for his contributions to the Club on and off the field during his time in Houston," Dynamo general manager Pat Onstad said in a statement. "He played a key role in the team winning the U.S. Open Cup in 2023 and setting a club points record in 2024. Erik approached us this summer and requested to pursue a new challenge outside of MLS. While the timing of his departure is not the most advantageous for the Club, we appreciated his tenure here, and we are supportive of his next competitive endeavor in Thailand."

After starting the first four games of the season, Sviatchenko has settled into a bench role this year for the Dynamo. Since Houston returned to action following the World Cup break, Sviatchenko has come off the bench twice and been an unused sub six times.

The Dynamo, currently second in the Western Conference standings, have five wins, two ties and one loss since returning in mid July.

Sviatchenko came to Houston from FC Midtjylland in Denmark , where he won the Danish Superliga Player of the Year award for the 2019-20 season.

Sviatchenko is the latest player to leave the Dynamo during the summer transfer window. Last month, forward Ezequiel Ponce moved to Elche CF in Spain and midfielder Ondřej Lingr departed for Korona Kielce. U.S. midfielder Jack McGlynn is also reportedly closing in on joining Stoke City in England .

Houston has signed striker Duncan McGuire and defender Marcelo Saracchi during the transfer window.

articles.body:
Talks between Olympique de Marseille and Crystal Palace for the transfer of Quinten Timber resumed on transfer deadline day. The Dutchman now looks set for a move to Selhurst Park, as per a report from RMC Sport.

Believing that the depth and quality of their midfield is sufficient, OM's management – who continue to seek funds to meet the financial constraints imposed by the National Directorate for Financial Control (DNCG) – are said to have opened the door to the departure of the Dutchman.

Talks regarding a transfer worth over €18m have been ongoing, alongside those being conducted by the Eagles – as well as Sunderland – in an attempt to finalise the deal for Malick Fofana (21). The Belgian could instead now be heading to the Black Cats.

Having joined OM from Feyenoord for €4.5m last winter, Timber has made 17 appearances in the white and blue since his arrival. RMC Sport now understands that Timber is close to completing a move to Crystal Palace with little time remaining before the closure of the transfer window.

articles.title: Blue Jays Make Long Series Of Lineup Changes Ahead of Biggest Series of Season vs. Guardians
articles.summary: We’re now into September, and things are getting serious for teams chasing a playoff spot. In the American League, the […]
articles.body:
We're now into September, and things are getting serious for teams chasing a playoff spot. In the American League, the last Wild Card berth is up for grabs, with as many as six teams in the wild scramble to try to claim it. Two of the frontrunners meet head-on for a three-game series starting Tuesday night, with the Toronto Blue Jays in Cleveland to take on the Guardians.

In preparation, the Jays have made a long series of moves to switch up their roster.

Former top prospect Ricky Tiedemann is back up with the big club, as is top minor league slugger Sean Keys. Additionally, left-hander Joe Mantiply has been activated from the 60-day IL and will be available out of the bullpen immediately. Infielder Josh Smith is also activated from IL.

The casualties are outfielder Daz Cameron, who has been designated for assignment, and Simeon Woods Richardson, who has cleared waivers and elected free agency.

Blue Jays add power bat and top pitching prospect to bullpen for September stretch run

Keys will add another power bat to the roster, certainly something the Jays can use. They currently rank 28th in MLB in Home Runs. Keys has 28 long balls in the high minors this season, with a 1.019 OPS. He got his feet wet in the majors back in July with 37 plate appearances. Some pop off the bench could certainly come in handy for Toronto.

Tiedemann was the Jays' No. 1 prospect just two years ago. But after missing a year and a half due to Tommy John surgery, he's back this season and is once again looking like he could help the major league team. He has posted a 3.75 ERA in 11 minor league appearances this year, striking out 12.8 batters per nine innings. The left-hander has been working out of the bullpen. Tiedemann made one appearance for the Jays two weeks ago, pitching 1.2 innings against the NY Yankees.

Going into this critical three-game set, Toronto sits only 1.5 games back (two in the loss column) of Cleveland for the third and final American League wild-card spot. The Jays are tied with the Texas Rangers at 68-70. The Baltimore Orioles are one game better and one back of the Guardians.

articles.title: 5 college football games to keep your eye on in Week 1
articles.summary: The 5 games you need to be keeping track of during Week 1.
articles.body:
College football is officially back, and after a handful of games took place last Saturday during Week 0, the rest of the country gets back on the field from Thursday to Monday during Week 1. It's the first full college football weekend of the season, and the long offseason is finally over.

Here at Sooners Wire, we'll certainly have our eyes all over the season-opening game for the Oklahoma Sooners , which will take place in Norman on Friday at 7 p.m. against the UTEP Miners. However, with a full slate of games for the first time since late November, there will be plenty of intriguing matchups to keep an eye on during Labor Day weekend.

Here are the top five games to watch in Week 1.

1. Louisville vs. Ole Miss , Sunday at 6:30 p.m. CT

Louisville and Ole Miss will face off at a neutral site at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee for the Liberty Mutual Music City Kickoff. The Cardinals are viewed as a dark horse team in the ACC heading into this season, and they'll have a big stage to make an early statement in non-league action. Head coach Jeff Brohm and quarterback Lincoln Kienholz will look to get off to a fast start in 2026.

On the other sideline, star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss leads the Rebels after a run in the College Football Playoff last year. It's Pete Golding's first full season as head coach, and his team has very high expectations this fall. The whole country will be watching, and the Rebs need to avoid the early setback.

2. Clemson at LSU, Saturday at 6:30 p.m. CT

For the second straight year, it's a battle of Tigers to open up the season, as Clemson and LSU will square off in Baton Rouge. Neither program met expectations last year, so this game is pivotal for both teams. A fast start is a must for both head coaches.

At Clemson, it's back to an underdog role for Dabo Swinney's squad, as he's named Christopher Vizzina as his new starting quarterback. In an unpredictable ACC, the Tigers are looking to prove they still run the league. For LSU, the Lane Kiffin show gets its start on Saturday night, as perhaps no figure in the sport makes as much noise as the Tigers' new coach. Transfer QB Sam Leavitt will be on a mission to help LSU start strong and claim which Death Valley reigns supreme in 2026.

3. Boise State at Oregon, Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT

Boise State and Oregon played an early-season thriller two years ago, and the rematch in Eugene might also be closer than most expect. The Broncos, led by veteran quarterback Maddux Madsen and superb head coach Spencer Danielson, are one of the favorites from the Group of Six to reach the CFP. They could turn the season on its head in Week 1 if they can pull off the upset.

The Ducks are one of the favorites to win the national title this year, as they are immensely talented and deep at every position. Head coach Dan Lanning gets star quarterback Dante Moore back this season, and the expectations are very high nationally for this team. They get a tough test very early in the season.

4. Baylor vs. Auburn , Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT

Baylor and Auburn will square off at a neutral site at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia, for the Aflac Kickoff. The Bears were defeated at home in this matchup to open the 2025 season, and they'll be hoping to return the favor to start a new season. Head coach Dave Aranda went out and got transfer QB DJ Lagway this offseason, and if he can recapture the magic he had in 2024 as a true freshman, Baylor will be in good shape.

It's a new era for the Tigers, as Alex Golesh takes over as the new head coach. In a loaded SEC, Auburn has a chance to make a statement or fall behind its peers very early on in Week 1. Luckily, transfer signal-caller Byrum Brown knows the offense very well and brings a lot of veteran production to the program.

5. UCLA at Cal, Saturday at 9:30 p.m. CT

UCLA and Cal have a lot in common as they enter the 2026 season. For the Bruins, new head coach Bob Chesney takes the reins, and he's ignited some excitement within the program for the first time in years. His quarterback returns, as Nico Iamaleava enters his second season in Los Angeles. In a top-heavy Big Ten, the Bruins will try and make some noise this season.

Similarly, the Golden Bears are also breaking in a new head coach, Tosh Lupoi. He has also helped bring excitement to the program, which hasn't had much in recent years. Cal also returns a big-name QB, with Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele staying in Berkley after a strong first season under center. This late-night game could determine a lot about the program's standing in the ACC this year.
